====Philadelphia Eagles====
On 13 January 2021, Siposs signed a reserve/futures contract with the [[Philadelphia Eagles]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=McPherson |first=Chris |date=13 January 2021 |title=Eagles sign P Arryn Siposs and WR Khalil Tate to Reserve/Futures contracts |url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-sign-p-arryn-siposs-and-wr-khalil-tate-to-reserve-futures-contracts |access-date=17 February 2021 |website=PhiladelphiaEagles.com}}</ref> Siposs made his NFL debut with the Eagles on 12 September against the [[2021 Atlanta Falcons season|Atlanta Falcons]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Zangaro |first=Dave |date=15 September 2021 |title=Why 'phenomenal' debut from Eagles punter didn't surprise his coach |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/philadelphia/eagles/eagles-punter-arryn-siposs-was-phenomenal-debut-michael-clay-says |access-date=28 January 2023 |website=NBC Sports}}</ref> In the 2021 season, Siposs recorded 55 punts for 2,416 yards for a 43.93 average.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Arryn Siposs 2021 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SipoAr01/gamelog/2021/ |access-date=22 February 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

During the 2022 season, Siposs injured his ankle in Week 14 and was placed on injured reserve.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Erby |first=Glenn |date=13 December 2022 |title=Eagles place punter Arryn Siposs on injured reserve |url=https://theeagleswire.usatoday.com/2022/12/13/philadelphia-eagles-news-arryn-siposs-injured-reseve-brett-kern-nfl-free-agency/ |access-date=22 February 2023 |website=Eagles Wire |language=en-US}}</ref> He recorded 44 punts for 2,005 total yards for a 45.57 average.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Arryn Siposs 2022 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SipoAr01/gamelog/2022/ |access-date=22 February 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He recovered in time to play in [[Super Bowl LVII]] against the [[Kansas City Chiefs]].<ref name="StuffNZ">{{Cite web |last=McCartney |first=Damien |date=14 February 2023|title=Diehard Philadelphia Eagles fans turn on Aussie Arryn Siposs after horror punt in Super Bowl loss|url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/nfl/300806379/diehard-philadelphia-eagles-fans-turn-on-aussie-arryn-siposs-after-horror-punt-in-super-bowl-loss|access-date=13 February 2023 |website=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]]}}</ref>  In Super Bowl LVII, Siposs punted twice. His second punt, occurring in the 4th quarter with the Eagles trailing by one point, was a low line drive that went in the wrong direction from where the [[Gunner (American football)|gunners]] were positioned.<ref name="StuffNZ" /> [[Kadarius Toney]] took advantage and returned the punt to the five-yard line, setting up a Kansas City [[touchdown]].<ref name="n234">{{cite web | last=Inabinett | first=Mark | title=Arryn Siposs on Super Bowl punt: 'It didn't work out in my favor' | website=AL.com| date=2023-02-22 | url=https://www.al.com/sports/2023/02/arryn-siposs-on-super-bowl-punt-it-didnt-work-out-in-my-favor.html | access-date=2025-01-10}}</ref> The Chiefs went on to win Super Bowl LVII by 3 points.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Super Bowl LVII - Philadelphia Eagles vs. Kansas City Chiefs - February 12th, 2023 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202302120phi.htm |access-date=22 February 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

On 29 August 2023, Siposs was waived by the Eagles and re-signed to the practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Spadaro |first1=Dave |last2=McPherson |first2=Chris |date=29 August 2023 |title=Eagles announce initial 53-man roster |url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-announce-initial-53-man-roster-2023 |access-date=2024-11-21 |website=PhiladelphiaEagles.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Boyle |first=Owen |date=30 August 2023 |title=Eagles announce practice squad |url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-announce-practice-squad-2023 |access-date=2024-11-21 |website=PhiladelphiaEagles.com}}</ref> On 18 September, Siposs was released from the Eagles' practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ulrich |first=Logan |date=18 September 2023 |title=Eagles Signing P Braden Mann To Practice Squad |url=https://nfltraderumors.co/eagles-signing-p-braden-mann-to-practice-squad/ |access-date=18 September 2023 |website=NFLTradeRumors.co |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Personal life==

Special teams coordinator & Running backs coach }} '''Armando Allen, Jr.''' (born April 30, 1989) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[running back]] for two seasons with the [[Chicago Bears]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish football|Notre Dame Fighting Irish]] and was signed by the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2011. He was the Running Backs Coach and Recruiting Coordinator for [[Charleston Southern University]] from 2019–2021. Allen previously held the position of assistant coach at [[Texas Southern University]]. ==Early life== Allen played [[high school football]] at [[Hialeah-Miami Lakes High School]] in [[Hialeah, Florida]]. A preseason fractured fibula ended his 2006 senior season before it ever began. However, he rushed for 1,095 yards and 12 [[Touchdown|touchdowns]] as junior in 2005, despite missing three games to injury. He was selected for 2007 [[U.S. Army All-American Bowl]] in San Antonio but did not participate because of his injury. Considered a four-star recruit by ''[[Rivals.com]]'', Allen was listed as the No. 2 all-purpose back in the nation.{{Cite web |title=Yahoo Sports: Rivals.com Ranking – Rivals.com all-purpose backs 2007 |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/football/recruiting/rankings/rank-1476;_ylt=AsDSZJxwepucAfxc.Mjf6gtGPZB4 |publisher=Rivals.yahoo.com |accessdate=August 3, 2012}} He chose Notre Dame over offers from [[Tennessee Volunteers football|Tennessee]], [[Duke Blue Devils football|Duke]] and [[Florida Gators football|Florida]]. ==College career== {{Unreferenced section|date=April 2026}} As a freshman, he started 4 games in which he recorded a team-best 1,176 all-purpose yards, averaging 98 yards per game.{{Citation needed|date=June 2025}} He was the second-leading rusher on the team with 348 yards on 86 carries. As a sophomore in 2008, he started 8 games in which he led the Irish in rushing with 585 yards on 134 carries (4.4 average) and added three touchdowns. He also ranked second on the team with 50 receptions and tallied 355 receiving yards and two touchdowns. As a junior, he only played in 8 games (7 starts) because of injury, but he was still able to lead the Irish in rushing for second straight season with 697 yards and three touchdowns on 142 carries. In his final season as a senior, playing in only 8 games due to a hip injury, ranked second on the team in rushing with 514 yards on 107 carries (4.8 average) and added two touchdowns. He finished his 4-year career at Notre Dame rushing for 2,144 yards on 469 carries (4.6 average) and 8 touchdowns. He lived up to the hype as being an all-purpose back, by recording 4337 all-purpose yards, which is fifth most in school history. He graduated with a degree in [[sociology]]. ==Professional career== {{NFL predraft | height ft = 5 | height in = 8 1/4 | weight = 199 | dash = 4.59 | ten split = 1.54 | twenty split = 2.64 | shuttle = 4.12 | cone drill = 7.10 | vertical = 31.5 | broad ft = 10 | broad in = 0 | bench = 23 | arm span = 30 1/4 | hand span = 8 3/4 | note = All values from [[NFL Combine]]/[[Pro Day]]{{Cite web |url=https://www.nfl.com/prospects/armando-allen/3200414c-4c05-9152-d13c-172d60e628a8 |title=Armando Allen Draft and Combine Prospect Profile |website=NFL.com |access-date=March 21, 2024}}{{Cite web |url=https://draftscout.com/dsprofile.php?PlayerId=68349&DraftYear=2011 |title=2011 NFL Draft Scout Armando Allen College Football Profile |website=DraftScout.com |access-date=March 21, 2024}} }} ===Tampa Bay Buccaneers=== Allen was signed by the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] on July 27, 2011.{{Cite web |last=Stroud |first=Rick |date=July 28, 2011 |title=Tampa Bay Buccaneers sign 16 undrafted free agents |url=http://www.tampabay.com/sports/football/bucs/tampa-bay-buccaneers-sign-16-undrafted-free-agents/1182837 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110809093247/http://www.tampabay.com/sports/football/bucs/tampa-bay-buccaneers-sign-16-undrafted-free-agents/1182837 |url-status=dead |archive-date=August 9, 2011 |website=[[St. Petersburg Times]] |accessdate=August 3, 2011}} However, he was waived during final cuts on September 3. ===Chicago Bears=== Allen was signed to the [[Chicago Bears]] [[practice squad]] on September 5, 2011. He was promoted to the active roster on December 19. Allen made his debut on Christmas Day against the [[Green Bay Packers]] and rushed for 40 yards on 11 carries.{{Cite web |date=December 23, 2011 |title=Allen likely to help fill void in backfield |url=http://www.chicagobears.com/news/NewsStory.asp?story_id=8502 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120107172458/http://www.chicagobears.com/news/NewsStory.asp?story_id=8502 |archive-date=January 7, 2012 |publisher=Chicagobears.com |accessdate=August 3, 2012}}{{Cite web |date=December 19, 2011 |title=Conte placed on IR; Bears promote three |url=http://www.chicagobears.com/news/NewsStory.asp?story_id=8490 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120314232128/http://www.chicagobears.com/news/NewsStory.asp?story_id=8490 |archive-date=March 14, 2012 |publisher=Chicagobears.com |accessdate=August 3, 2012}} Allen lost the third running back battle to [[Lorenzo Booker]], and was waived on August 31, 2012. Allen scored his first career touchdown run against the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] on October 7, 2012, the longest touchdown run by a Bears player since [[Matt Forte]]'s 68-yard run in 2010. Though he became an exclusive rights free agent in 2013, Allen signed his tender on March 28.{{Cite web |last=Mayer |first=Larry |date=March 28, 2013 |title=Armando Allen signs exclusive rights tender |url=http://www.chicagobears.com/news/article-1/Armando-Allen-signs-exclusive-rights-tender/55b85535-06a8-4fe1-8f36-28b992961576 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130426140459/http://www.chicagobears.com/news/article-1/Armando-Allen-signs-exclusive-rights-tender/55b85535-06a8-4fe1-8f36-28b992961576 |archive-date=April 26, 2013 |publisher=[[Chicago Bears]] |accessdate=March 28, 2013}} He was released on August 30, 2013. ==References== {{Reflist|30em}} ==External links== * [http://www.und.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/allenjr_armando00.html Notre Dame Fighting Irish bio] * [https://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/14358/armando-allen ESPN.com bio] {{DEFAULTSORT:Allen, Armando}} [[Category:1989 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Players of American football from Miami-Dade County, Florida]] [[Category:Hialeah-Miami Lakes Senior High School alumni]] [[Category:American football running backs]] [[Category:Notre Dame Fighting Irish football players]] [[Category:Tampa Bay Buccaneers players]] [[Category:Chicago Bears players]] [[Category:Texas Southern Tigers football coaches]]

'''Armond Smith''' (born May 7, 1986) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[running back]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Union (Kentucky) Bulldogs football|Union Bulldogs]].

==College football==
Smith played [[college football]] at [[Union College (Kentucky)|Union College]] in [[Barbourville, Kentucky]].

==Professional football==
===Cleveland Browns===
Smith was signed by the [[Cleveland Browns]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2011.  Smith was first noticed when he ran an 81-yard touchdown in the 2011 preseason against the [[Detroit Lions]].

===Carolina Panthers===
Smith was ejected from a preseason game against the [[Baltimore Ravens]] on August 22, 2013 for the act of kicking second-string linebacker, [[Albert McClellan]] in the groin after the whistle.<ref>{{cite news| url=http://ftw.usatoday.com/2013/08/panthers-ravens-groin-kick-ejected/ | work=USA Today | title=Panthers RB ejected for kicking opponent in the groin}}</ref>

===Toronto Argonauts===
On October 14, 2014, Smith signed a practice roster agreement with the [[Toronto Argonauts]] of the [[Canadian Football League]]. He was released by the Argonauts on November 11, 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.argonauts.ca/page/2014-transactions |title=2014 TRANSACTIONS |publisher=argonauts.ca |accessdate=November 21, 2014 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140802132312/http://argonauts.ca/page/2014-transactions |archivedate=August 2, 2014 }}</ref>

{{Short description|American gridiron football player (born 1990)}} {{Use mdy dates|date=July 2024}} {{Infobox NFL biography | name = Armond Armstead | image = | caption = | number = 97 | status = | cflstatus = import | position = [[Defensive tackle]] | birth_date = {{birth date and age|1990|8|3}} | birth_place = [[Sacramento, California]], U.S. | death_date = | death_place = | height_ft = 6 | height_in = 5 | weight_lbs = 305 | high_school = [[Pleasant Grove High School (California)|Pleasant Grove]]
([[Elk Grove, California]]) | college = [[USC Trojans football|USC]] | undraftedyear = 2012 | pastteams = * [[Toronto Argonauts]] ({{CFL Year|2012}}) * [[New England Patriots]] ({{NFL Year|2013}}) | highlights = * [[Grey Cup]] champion ([[100th Grey Cup|2012]]) * [[Canadian Football League|CFL]] All-Star ({{CFL Year|2012}}) * [[Canadian Football League|CFL]] East All-Star ({{CFL Year|2012}}) | cflstatlabel1 = [[Tackle (football move)|Total tackles]] | cflstatvalue1 = 43 | cflstatlabel2 = [[Quarterback sack|Sacks]] | cflstatvalue2 = 6.0 | cfl-archive = https://web.archive.org/web/20150930125637/http://www.cfl.ca/roster/show/id/5317 }} '''Armond Armstead''' (born August 3, 1990) is a former [[defensive tackle]] for the [[Toronto Argonauts]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL) and the [[New England Patriots]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] at [[USC Trojans football|USC]]. He was signed by the Argonauts as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2012. ==High school football== Armstead played high school football at [[Pleasant Grove High School (California)|Pleasant Grove High]] in [[Elk Grove, California]].{{Cite web |date=2015-05-01 |title=Elk Grove's Arik Armstead Looks To Take The NFL Path His Brother Didn't Get - CBS Sacramento |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/sacramento/news/elk-groves-erik-armstead-looks-to-take-the-nfl-path-his-brother-didnt-get/ |access-date=2025-04-17 |website=www.cbsnews.com |language=en-US}}{{Cite web |date=2012-08-31 |title=Former USC football player from Elk Grove sues over injected drug |url=https://www.kcra.com/article/former-usc-football-player-from-elk-grove-sues-over-injected-drug/6398789 |access-date=2025-04-17 |website=KCRA |language=en}} His honors included Super Prep All-American, Prep Star All-American, Super Prep All-Farwest, Prep Star All-West, Long Beach ''[[Press-Telegram]]'' Best in the West honorable mention, Tacoma [[The News Tribune|''News Tribune'']] Western 100, Cal-Hi Sports All-State first team, All-Northern California, ''Sacramento Bee'' All-Metro and All-Metro League MVP as a senior defensive and offensive lineman at Pleasant Grove High in Elk Grove (Calif.). He had 88 tackles and 11 sacks in 2007. As a junior in 2006, he had 79 tackles and 5 sacks.{{cite web|url=http://www.usctrojans.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/armstead_armond00.html|title=Armond Armstead Bio - University of Southern California Official Athletic Site|publisher=usctrojans.com|accessdate=8 May 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170526093356/http://www.usctrojans.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/armstead_armond00.html|archive-date=26 May 2017|url-status=dead}} ==College football== Armstead attended the [[University of Southern California]], playing three seasons from 2008 to 2010, starting 17 games and recording 59 tackles.Pedro Moura, [https://www.espn.com/los-angeles/ncf/story/_/id/8320090/former-usc-trojans-de-armond-armstead-sues-school-painkiller Armond Armstead sues USC], ESPNLosAngeles.com, August 30, 2012, accessed January 23, 2013. However after an initially undisclosed injury, USC's staff refused to medically clear him to play in 2011. He later sued the school, accusing team doctors of giving him painkillers ([[Toradol]]) that caused a [[heart attack]] and damaged his future earning potential. He went undrafted in the [[2012 NFL draft]].Mike Reiss and Mike Rodak, [https://www.espn.com/boston/nfl/story/_/id/8870230/armond-armstead-signs-new-england-patriots-according-sources Sources: Pats sign Armond Armstead], ESPNBoston.com, January 22, 2013, accessed January 23, 2013. ==Professional football== ===Toronto Argonauts=== In 2012, Armstead was signed by the [[Toronto Argonauts]] of the [[Canadian Football League]]. In his rookie CFL season, Armstead compiled 43 defensive tackles, 2 special teams tackles, and 6 quarterback sacks. He was also named as a CFL All-star, and went on to win the [[100th Grey Cup]] with the Argonauts that season. On January 4, 2013, Armstead was released by the Argonauts per request in order to pursue an NFL career. ===New England Patriots=== On January 22, 2013, he signed with the New England Patriots. Per the terms of the [[NFL Collective Bargaining Agreement]], the Patriots were required to sign Armstead, an undrafted free agent, to a three-year deal at the standard salaries of $405,000 for 2013, $495,000 for 2014, and $585,000 in 2015. While the contract did not include a signing bonus, nearly half the contract was guaranteed: his entire salary for 2013 is guaranteed, and $250,000 of his 2014 salary.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/boston/new-england-patriots/post/_/id/4739148/armstead-gets-655k-guaranteed|title=Armstead gets $655K guaranteed|work=ESPN.com|date=23 January 2013 |access-date=8 May 2016}} On July 29, 2013, Armstead underwent surgery to treat an undisclosed infection. On August 26, 2013, he was placed on the reserve/non-football injury list.{{cite web |url=http://nesn.com/2013/08/patriots-release-kamar-aiken-niko-koutouvides-three-others-re-sign-two-players/ |title=Patriots Release Kamar Aiken, Niko Koutouvides, Three Others, Re-Sign Two players |last=Hughes |first=Luke |date=August 26, 2013 |website=NESN.com |accessdate=September 4, 2013}} On July 16, 2014, he announced his retirement from football at the age of 23.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/boston/nfl/story/_/id/11224120/armond-armstead-new-england-patriots-retires|title=Armond Armstead of New England Patriots retires|work=[[ESPN.com]]|date=16 July 2014 |access-date=8 May 2016}}{{cite web|url=http://www.cbssports.com/nfl/eye-on-football/24624016/patriots-first-year-dl-armond-armstead-retires|title=Patriots first-year DL Armond Armstead retires|work=[[CBSSports.com]]|accessdate=8 May 2016}} ==Personal life== Armstead's brother, [[Arik Armstead]], played college football at Oregon and is currently on the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]]. ==References== {{reflist|30em}} ==External links== *[https://web.archive.org/web/20130310000639/http://argonauts.ca/roster/show/id/5317 Toronto Argonauts bio] *[https://web.archive.org/web/20170526093356/http://www.usctrojans.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/armstead_armond00.html USC Trojans bio] {{100th Grey Cup}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Armstead, Armond}} [[Category:1990 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:American football defensive ends]] [[Category:American football defensive tackles]] [[Category:Canadian football defensive linemen]] [[Category:Toronto Argonauts players]] [[Category:USC Trojans football players]] [[Category:Players of American football from Sacramento, California]] [[Category:Players of Canadian football from Sacramento, California]] [[Category:Pleasant Grove High School (California) alumni]]

'''Armonty Charles Bryant''' (born May 20, 1990) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive end]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[NCAA Division II|Division II]] [[East Central Tigers football|East Central Tigers]] of [[Ada, Oklahoma]]. He was selected by the [[Cleveland Browns]] in the seventh round of the [[2013 NFL draft]].

==Professional career==
===Cleveland Browns===
On April 27, 2013, Bryant was selected by the [[Cleveland Browns]] in the seventh round, 217th overall pick of the [[2013 NFL draft]].<ref>{{cite web | title=Cleveland Browns pick DE Armonty Bryant in the 7th round NFL Draft 2013 | work=cleveland.com | url=https://www.cleveland.com/browns/index.ssf/2013/04/cleveland_browns_pick_in_the_7.html |accessdate=April 27, 2013}}</ref>

He was suspended for the first four games of the [[2016 NFL season|2016 season]] for violating the performance-enhancing drug policy.<ref>{{cite web|work=ESPN.com|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/14903270/cleveland-browns-linebacker-armonty-bryant-suspended-4-games-ped-violation|title=Browns LB Armonty Bryant suspended 4 games for PEDs|date=March 4, 2016|first=Pat|last=McManamon|access-date=March 25, 2016}}</ref> He was released by the Browns on October 3, 2016.<ref>{{cite web|title=Browns release LB Armonty Bryant|url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-release-lb-armonty-bryant-17808673|website=ClevelandBrowns.com|date=October 1, 2016}}</ref>

===Detroit Lions===
On October 4, 2016, Bryant was claimed off waivers by the Lions.<ref>{{cite web|title=Lions awarded DE Armonty Bryant via waivers|url=https://www.detroitlions.com/news/lions-awarded-de-armonty-bryant-via-waivers-17819342|website=DetroitLions.com|date=October 4, 2016}}</ref> Bryant had to serve another three-game suspension for violating the league's policy on substances of abuse.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/lions-armonty-bryant-suspended-three-games-0ap3000000732276|title=Lions' Armonty Bryant suspended three games|last=Bergman|first=Jeremy|date=November 1, 2016|work=NFL.com|language=en}}</ref> He was activated on December 3, prior to Week 13.<ref>{{cite web|title=Lions sign WR TJ Jones to active roster and activate DE Armonty Bryant|url=https://www.detroitlions.com/news/lions-sign-wr-tj-jones-to-active-roster-and-activate-de-armonty-bryant-18195542|website=DetroitLions.com|date=December 3, 2016}}</ref> He was placed on injured reserve on December 6 with a knee injury.<ref>{{cite web|title=Lions sign RB Joique Bell and CB Asa Jackson|url=https://www.detroitlions.com/news/lions-sign-rb-joique-bell-and-cb-asa-jackson-18216235|website=DetroitLions.com|date=December 4, 2016}}</ref>

On March 21, 2017, Bryant re-signed with the Lions.<ref>{{cite web|title=Lions re-sign DE Armonty Bryant|url=https://www.detroitlions.com/news/lions-re-sign-de-armonty-bryant-18670455|website=DetroitLions.com|date=March 21, 2017}}</ref> He was suspended once again for the first four games of the [[2017 NFL season]] for violating the NFL's substance abuse policy.<ref>{{cite web|title=Detroit Lions' Armonty Bryant suspended four games|url=http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000820530/article/detroit-lions-de-armonty-bryant-suspended-four-games|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171004090253/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000820530/article/detroit-lions-de-armonty-bryant-suspended-four-games|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 4, 2017|website=NFL.com|date=July 18, 2017}}</ref> On October 9, 2017, after being re-instated from suspension, Bryant was released by the Lions.<ref>{{cite web|title=Detroit Lions release DE Armonty Bryant|url=https://www.prideofdetroit.com/2017/10/9/16449322/detroit-lions-release-armonty-bryant-suspension-over|website=PrideOfDetroit.com|date=October 9, 2017}}</ref>

===Oakland Raiders===
On April 6, 2018, Bryant signed with the [[Oakland Raiders]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Raiders Sign DE Armonty Bryant|url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-sign-de-armonty-bryant-20519665|website=Raiders.com|date=April 6, 2018}}</ref> On May 4, 2018, he was waived by the Raiders with a non-football illness designation.<ref name="h779">{{cite web | last=Damien | first=Levi | title=Raiders waive Cory James, cut Armonty Bryant | website=Silver And Black Pride | date=2018-05-04 | url=https://www.silverandblackpride.com/2018/5/4/17320934/raiders-waive-cory-james-cut-armonty-bryant | access-date=2025-02-17}}</ref>

===Retirement===
On July 16, 2018, Bryant announced his retirement from the NFL.<ref>{{cite web|title=Former NFL DE Armonty Bryant announces retirement|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/former-nfl-de-armonty-bryant-announces-retirement/|website=CBSSports.com|date=July 16, 2018}}</ref>

==Personal life==
In October 2012, Bryant pleaded [[Nolo contendere|no contest]] following an arrest for selling marijuana twice in a parking lot at [[East Central University]], receiving probation from October 18, 2012, to October 18, 2017.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.kxii.com/home/headlines/ECU-football-player-pleads-no-contest-to-drug-charge-176186411.html|title=ECU football player pleads no contest to drug charge|last=Humphrey|first=Sara|date=October 28, 2012|work=KXII News 12|access-date=October 4, 2017|archive-date=October 4, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171004085610/http://www.kxii.com/home/headlines/ECU-football-player-pleads-no-contest-to-drug-charge-176186411.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> In May 2013, he was given a one-year deferred sentence after he pleaded no contest to a charge of [[driving under the influence]] of alcohol.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/browns-armonty-bryant-arrested-charged-with-dui-0ap1000000167322|title=Browns' Armonty Bryant arrested, charged with DUI|last=Wesseling|first=Chris|date=May 6, 2013|work=NFL.com}}</ref> Bryant was indicted on two felony drug possession charges in February 2016 after being arrested following a traffic stop on December 25, 2015, for speeding. During a search of the vehicle, [[Ohio Highway Patrol]] officers discovered two pills of [[Oxycodone]] and one [[Adderall]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/14754426/cleveland-browns-armonty-bryant-former-player-deante-saunders-indicted|title=Browns DE Bryant indicted on felony drug charges|last=McManamon|first=Pat|date=February 10, 2016|work=ESPN.com}}</ref>

As of February 2019, Bryant is being treated for [[focal segmental glomerulosclerosis]] (FSGS), which has led to [[kidney failure]] and requires [[Kidney dialysis|dialysis]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/26047187/i-need-kidney-nfl-pass-rusher-dialysis-year |title='I need a kidney': From NFL pass-rusher to dialysis in a year |first=Michael |last=Rothstein |website=[[ESPN]] |date=February 24, 2019 |access-date=February 24, 2019}}</ref>

He was selected by the 49ers in the fifth round of the [[1981 NFL draft]] after playing [[college football]] for the [[Winston-Salem State Rams football|Winston-Salem State Rams]]. ==Early life== Jones attended [[John Marshall High School (Richmond, Virginia)|John Marshall High School]] in [[Richmond, Virginia]].{{cite web |url=http://www.profootballarchives.com/jone01000.html |title=ARRINGTON JONES |publisher=profootballarchives.com |access-date=July 29, 2015 |archive-date=August 27, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160827174450/http://www.profootballarchives.com/jone01000.html |url-status=dead }} Jones played for the [[Winston-Salem State Rams football|Winston-Salem State Rams]] of [[Winston-Salem State University]] from 1978 to 1981.{{cite web|url=http://www.richmond.com/sports/article_d4eb7bd0-4636-5dbc-aaa7-5b317ce0a5f2.html |title=Arrington Jones file |publisher=richmond.com |date=November 28, 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200511172821/https://www.richmond.com/sports/article_d4eb7bd0-4636-5dbc-aaa7-5b317ce0a5f2.html |archive-date=May 11, 2020 |url-status=dead |access-date=August 27, 2016 }} ==Professional career== Jones was selected by the [[San Francisco 49ers]] of the NFL with the 122nd pick in the [[1981 NFL draft]]. He fumbled two kickoff returns in the opening game of the 1981 season at Detroit. He was released after that game and never played another NFL game.{{cite web | url=http://www.profootballarchives.com/transactions/j/jone01000.html | title=Arrington Jones Transactions | publisher=Pro Football Archives | accessdate=2 June 2025}} Jones signed with the [[Denver Broncos]] on February 12, 1982. He was released on July 21, 1982, after failing a physical. On November 3, 1982, Jones was signed by the USFL's [[Washington Federals]] for the [[1983 USFL season]]. He was released by the Federals on February 22, 1983.{{cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/sports/1983/02/22/federals-cut-12-from-roster/e85b0bf4-0504-4379-8066-1cbd03971179/ |title=Federals Cut 12 From Roster |work=[[the Washington Post]] |date=February 22, 1983 |author=Remnick, David |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20160827111837/https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/sports/1983/02/22/federals-cut-12-from-roster/e85b0bf4-0504-4379-8066-1cbd03971179/ |archive-date=August 27, 2016 |access-date=August 27, 2016 }} Jones signed with the 49ers again on April 1, 1983. He was later released on August 10, 1983. Jones signed with the [[Indianapolis Colts]] on May, 25, 1984, but was later released. ==Coaching career== Jones served as [[special teams coordinator]] for the [[Virginia State Trojans football|Virginia State Trojans]] of [[Virginia State University]] from to 1986 to 1990. He was also [[assistant head coach]] and [[offensive coordinator]] from 1990 to 2000. The Trojans won the [[Central Intercollegiate Athletic Association|CIAA]] Championship in 1995.{{cite web|url=http://www.dsuhornets.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=12900&ATCLID=205144522 |title=Arrington Jones |publisher=dsuhornets.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160531033846/http://www.dsuhornets.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=205144522&DB_OEM_ID=12900 |archive-date=May 31, 2016 |access-date=August 27, 2016 }} He was offensive coordinator and recruiting coordinator for the Winston-Salem State Rams from 2001 to 2003. The Rams appeared in the CIAA Championship Game in 2001. Jones served as [[head coach]] and offensive coordinator for the [[Virginia Union Panthers football|Virginia Union Panthers]] of [[Virginia Union University]] from 2004 to 2007, accruing a 21–21 record.{{cite web|url=http://onnidan.com/07-08/news/march/vuufb0325.htm |title=Arrington Jones resigns as Va Union head football coach |publisher=onnidan.com |date=March 25, 2008 |access-date=July 29, 2015 |url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150729170914/http://onnidan.com/07-08/news/march/vuufb0325.htm |archive-date=July 29, 2015 }}{{cite web|url=http://www.cfbdatawarehouse.com/data/active/v/virginia_union/2000-2004_yearly_results.php |title=Virginia Union Yearly Results |publisher=cfbdatawarehouse.com |access-date=July 29, 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150729185147/http://www.cfbdatawarehouse.com/data/active/v/virginia_union/2000-2004_yearly_results.php |archive-date=July 29, 2015 }}{{cite web|url=http://www.cfbdatawarehouse.com/data/active/v/virginia_union/2005-2009_yearly_results.php |title=Virginia Union Yearly Results |publisher=cfbdatawarehouse.com |access-date=July 29, 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150729185146/http://www.cfbdatawarehouse.com/data/active/v/virginia_union/2005-2009_yearly_results.php |archive-date=July 29, 2015 }} He led the Panthers to a 9–1 regular season record in 2007, winning the CIAA Eastern Division Championship. {{Short description|American football player (1972–2022)}} {{Use mdy dates|date=March 2022}} {{Infobox NFL biography | name = Arnold Mickens | image = | number = 27 | position = [[Running back]] | birth_date = {{birth date|1972|10|12}} | birth_place = [[Indianapolis, Indiana]], U.S. | death_date = {{Death date and age|2022|01|18|1972|10|12}} | death_place = Indianapolis, Indiana, U.S. | height_ft = 5 | height_in = 11 | weight_lbs = 217 | high_school = [[Broad Ripple High School|Broad Ripple]] (Indianapolis) | college = [[Indiana Hoosiers football|Indiana]] (1991–1993)
[[Butler Bulldogs football|Butler]] (1994–1995) | undraftedyear = 1996 | pastteams = * [[Indianapolis Colts]] ({{NFL Year|1996}}–{{NFL Year|1997}}) | pfr = M/MickAr20 }} '''Arnold Lee Mickens Jr.''' (October 12, 1972 – January 18, 2022) was an American professional [[American football|football]] [[running back]] who played one season with the [[Indianapolis Colts]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] at [[Indiana University Bloomington]] and [[Butler University]]. ==Early life== Arnold Lee Mickens Jr. was born on October 12, 1972, in [[Indianapolis, Indiana]].{{cite web | url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/players/m/mick00630.html | title=Arnold Mickens | publisher=profootballarchives.com | accessdate=24 December 2024}} He attended [[Broad Ripple High School]] in Indianapolis. He was a [[linebacker]] and running back on the football team at Broad Ripple High, earning all-state honors.{{Cite web |last=VanTryon |first=Matthew |date=January 20, 2022 |title=Arnold Mickens, Broad Ripple grad who took college football by storm at Butler, dies at 49 |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/2022/01/20/arnold-mickens-butler-football-broad-ripple-colts-indianapolis-public-schools/6591183001/ |access-date=2022-06-23 |website=The Indianapolis Star |language=en-US}} ==College career== Mickens was a member of the [[Indiana Hoosiers football|Indiana Hoosiers]] of the [[Indiana University Bloomington]] from 1991 to 1993 and a two-year [[letterman (sports)|letterman]] from 1992 to 1993. He [[redshirted]] the 1991 season, and played several positions on the [[scout team]]. He was converted to linebacker full-time in 1992 and started one game that year, recording 34 tackles and one sack. He garnered [[Big Ten]] all-academic team recognition in 1992. He played in seven games in 1993, posting four tackles. Mickens then transferred to play for the [[Butler Bulldogs football|Butler Bulldogs]] of [[Butler University]], where he was a two-year letterman at running back from 1994 to 1995. He rushed for an [[NCAA Division I-AA]] record 2,255 yards in 1994.{{cite web | url=https://www.si.com/college/fcs/top-single-season-rushing-performances-in-fcs-football-history | title=Top Single-Season Rushing Performances In FCS Football History | publisher=si.com | date=May 15, 2024 | accessdate=24 December 2024 | author=Rosario, Timothy}} He rushed for over 200 yards in an NCAA Division I-AA record eight straight games in 1994 as well. Mickens also set NCA Division I-AA records in single-game rushing attempts with 56, most consecutive rushing attempts by the same player with 26, and career rushing yards per game with 190.7.{{cite web | url=https://www.ncaa.com/news/football/article/2024-11-30/7-most-unbreakable-records-fcs-football-history#:~:text=Arnold%20Mickens'%208%20straight%20200%2Dyard%20rushing%20games%20%7C%201994&text=Among%20Mickens'%20FCS%20single%2Dseason,yards%20per%20game%20(190.7). | title=7 of the most unbreakable records in FCS football history | publisher=ncaa.com | date=November 30, 2024 | accessdate=24 December 2024 | author=Chiusano, Anthony}} He majored in public and corporate communications at Butler.{{cite news | url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/sports/1994/10/21/butlers-mickens-runs-on-his-terms/82b878e2-7e0f-4c4a-987f-13fa67b2fbc0/ | title=BUTLER'S MICKENS RUNS ON HIS TERMS | work=[[The Washington Post]] | date=October 20, 1994 | accessdate=24 December 2024 | author=Montieth, Mark}} He was inducted into Butler's athletics hall of fame in 2009.{{cite web | url=https://indianapolisrecorder.com/arnold-mickens-showed-patience-perseverance-through-storied-football-career/ | title='His calling was to love': Arnold Mickens lives on in football record books and classrooms | publisher=indianapolisrecorder.com | date=January 21, 2022 | accessdate=24 December 2024 | author=Fenwick, Tyler}} He was a member of [[Phi Beta Sigma]] fraternity.{{Cite web|title=XI SIGMA ALUMNI CHAPTER OF CENTRAL INDIANA OF PHI BETA SIGMA FRATERNITY INC. :: Indiana (US) :: OpenCorporates|url=https://opencorporates.com/companies/us_in/2008091800020|access-date=January 19, 2022|website=opencorporates.com}} ==Professional career== After going undrafted in the [[1996 NFL draft]], Mickens signed with the [[Indianapolis Colts]] on April 26. He was released on August 28, signed to the team's practice squad on September 10, released again on September 23, and signed to the practice squad again on October 15. He was promoted to the active roster on October 18 and played in three games (primarily on special teams) for the Colts before being released on November 12.{{cite web | url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/MickAr20/gamelog/1996/ | title=Arnold Mickens 1996 Game Log | publisher=pro-football-reference.com | accessdate=24 December 2024}} Mickens was signed to the practice squad the next day. He signed a futures contract with the Colts on January 6, 1997.{{cite web | url=https://www.prosportstransactions.com/football/Search/SearchResults.php?Player=Arnold+Mickens&Team=&BeginDate=&EndDate=&PlayerMovementChkBx=yes&submit=Search | title=Search Results | publisher=prosportstransactions.com | accessdate=24 December 2024}} He was released on July 18, 1997, after failing a physical.{{cite web | url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/transactions/m/mick00630.html | title=Arnold Mickens NFL Transactions | publisher=profootballarchives.com | accessdate=24 December 2024}} He was later waived on March 11, 1998. ==Personal life== Mickens later worked as a counselor in the Indianapolis Public Schools system. He died on January 18, 2022, in Indianapolis at the age of 49. ==References== {{reflist}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Mickens, Arnold}} [[Category:1972 births]] [[Category:2022 deaths]] [[Category:Players of American football from Indianapolis]] [[Category:American football running backs]] [[Category:American football linebackers]] [[Category:Indiana Hoosiers football players]] [[Category:Butler Bulldogs football players]] [[Category:Indianapolis Colts players]] [[Category:20th-century American sportsmen]] [[Category:20th-century African-American sportsmen]]

{{Short description|American football player (1953–2014)}} {{Use mdy dates|date=June 2024}} {{Infobox NFL biography | name = Art Best | image = | number = 25, 39 | position = [[Running back]] | birth_date = {{birth date|1953|3|18}} | birth_place = [[Camden, New Jersey]], U.S. | death_date = {{death date and age|2014|10|14|1953|3|18}} | death_place = [[Pickerington, Ohio]], U.S. | height_ft = 6 | height_in = 1 | weight_lbs = 205 | high_school = [[Bishop Hartley High School (Columbus, Ohio)|Bishop Hartley]]
([[Columbus, Ohio]]) | college = [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish football|Notre Dame]] (1972–1974)
[[Kent State Golden Flashes football|Kent State]] (1976) | draftyear = 1977 | draftround = 6 | draftpick = 156 | pastteams = * [[Chicago Bears]] ({{NFL Year|1977}}–{{NFL Year|1978}}) * [[New York Giants]] ({{NFL Year|1980}}) |highlights= * National champion ([[1973 Notre Dame Fighting Irish football team|1973]]) | pfr = B/BestAr20 }} '''Arthur Robie Best''' (March 18, 1953 – October 14, 2014) was an American professional [[American football|football]] [[running back]] who played three seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) with the [[Chicago Bears]] and [[New York Giants]]. He was selected by the [[Los Angeles Rams]] in the sixth round of the [[1977 NFL draft]]. He played [[college football]] at the [[University of Notre Dame]] and [[Kent State University]]. ==Early life== Arthur Robie Best was born on March 18, 1953, in [[Camden, New Jersey]].{{cite web | url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/players/b/best00200.html | title=Art Best | publisher=profootballarchives.com | accessdate=24 December 2024}} He grew up in [[Gahanna, Ohio]] and attended [[Bishop Hartley High School (Columbus, Ohio)|Bishop Hartley High School]] in [[Columbus, Ohio]]. ==College career== Best first played [[college football]] for the [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish football|Notre Dame Fighting Irish]] of the [[University of Notre Dame]] from 1972 to 1974. He rushed 17 times for 158 yards and two touchdowns in 1972. In 1973, he totaled 118 carries for 700 yards and three touchdowns, and four catches for 48 yards. The [[1973 Notre Dame Fighting Irish football team|1973 Fighting Irish]] were [[AP Poll]] national champions. Best recorded 51 rushing attempts for 241 yards and three receptions for 54 yards in 1974. Best then transferred to [[Kent State University]], where he [[letterman (sports)|lettered]] for the [[Kent State Golden Flashes football|Kent State Golden Flashes]] in 1976. He rushed 194 times for 1,030 yards and ten touchdowns that season while also returning six kicks for 102 yards.{{cite web | url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/art-best-1.html | title=Art Best | publisher=sports-reference.com | accessdate=24 December 2024}} ==Professional career== Best was selected by the [[Los Angeles Rams]] in the sixth round, with the 156th overall pick, of the [[1977 NFL draft]], and thereafter signed with the team. On October 7, 1977, he was traded to the [[Chicago Bears]]. He played in all 14 games for the Bears during his rookie year in 1977, recording six carries for 20 yards and six kick returns for 127 yards.{{cite web | url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BestAr20.htm | title=Art Best | publisher=pro-football-reference.com | accessdate=24 December 2024}} He also played in one playoff game that season. He appeared in all 16 games in 1978, rushing two times for 11 yards. Best was released by the Bears on August 27, 1979. Best signed with the [[New York Giants]] on March 1, 1980. He played in the first game of the 1980 season before being released on September 8, 1980.{{cite web | url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BestAr20/gamelog/1980/ | title=Art Best | publisher=pro-football-reference.com | accessdate=24 December 2024}}{{cite web | url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/transactions/b/best00200.html | title=Art Best NFL Transactions | publisher=profootballarchives.com | accessdate=24 December 2024}} ==Personal life== Best worked as a construction project manager after his NFL career. He died on October 14, 2014, in [[Pickerington, Ohio]]. He had cancer and liver problems for at least five years before his death.{{cite web | url=http://www.dispatch.com/content/stories/sports/2014/10/17/art-best-obit.html | title=Art Best, former Hartley and Notre Dame football star, dies at 61 | publisher=dispatch.com | date=October 17, 2014 | access-date=December 2, 2014}} ==References== {{reflist}} ==External links== *[https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/art-best-1.html College stats] {{1973 Notre Dame Fighting Irish football navbox}} {{Los Angeles Rams 1977 draft navbox}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Best, Art}} [[Category:1953 births]] [[Category:2014 deaths]] [[Category:Players of American football from Louisiana]] [[Category:American football running backs]] [[Category:Notre Dame Fighting Irish football players]] [[Category:Kent State Golden Flashes football players]] [[Category:Chicago Bears players]] [[Category:New York Giants players]] [[Category:Players of American football from Camden, New Jersey]] [[Category:20th-century American sportsmen]]

'''Arie-Manuel Kouandjio''' (born April 23, 1992) is a [[Cameroon]]ian former professional player of [[American football]] who was a [[Guard (gridiron football)|guard]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Alabama Crimson Tide football|Alabama Crimson Tide]], and was selected by the [[Washington Redskins]] in the fourth round of the [[2015 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Georgette and Jean-Claude Kouandjio, Arie's mother and father, immigrated to the United States from [[Cameroon]] in 1998 when he was six years old.<ref name="ArieCitizenship">{{Cite web |last=Sabin |first=Rainer |date=2016-09-13 |title=As fellow NFL players sit for anthem, former Alabama OL proud to become an American |url=https://www.al.com/alabamafootball/2016/09/as_fellow_nfl_players_sit_for.html |access-date=2024-10-03 |website=AL.com}}</ref>

Kouandjio initially attended [[High Point High School]] in [[Beltsville, Maryland]], where he played [[high school football|football]] for the Eagles program. After his sophomore year he was recruited and transferred to [[DeMatha Catholic High School]] in [[Hyattsville, Maryland]] along with his younger brother [[Cyrus Kouandjio|Cyrus]], where he played football for the Stags program.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 2, 2015 |title=Arie Kouandjio #60 OG |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/ariekouandjio/2552333/profile |access-date=March 30, 2019 |website=NFL}}</ref> He was a four-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Rivals.com |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/ncaa/football/recruiting/player-Arie-Kouandjio-93907 |website=sports.yahoo.com}}</ref> In February 2010, he committed to the [[University of Alabama]] to play [[college football]].<ref name="p538">{{cite web | last=Estes | first=Gentry | title=Offensive line recruit Arie Kouandjio set to sign with Alabama | website=AL.com| date=2010-02-03 | url=https://www.al.com/bamabeat/2010/02/ol_recruit_arie_kouandjio_set.html | access-date=2024-10-03}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Bone |first=Andrew |title=ANDREW BONE: Arie Kouandjio Picks Bama |url=http://www.tuscaloosanews.com/article/20100202/news/100209891}}</ref>

==College career==
Kouandjio was [[redshirted]] as a true freshman in 2010. As a redshirt freshman in 2011, he played in two games before a knee injury ended his season.<ref name="a044">{{cite web | last=Kausler Jr. | first=Don| title=Tide injury update: Arie Kouandjio might need season-ending knee surgery | website=AL.com| date=2011-10-10 | url=https://www.al.com/sports/2011/10/tide_injury_update_arie_kouand.html | access-date=2024-10-03}}</ref> As a sophomore in 2012, Kouandjio played in 11 of 14 games as a backup.<ref name="y499">{{cite web | last=Kausler Jr. | first=Don | title=Get to know Tide lineman Arie Kouandjio, who wants to start next to his brother | website=AL.com| date=2013-03-13 | url=https://www.al.com/alabamafootball/2013/03/get_to_know_tide_lineman_arie.html | access-date=2024-10-03}}</ref> He became a starter for the first time as junior in 2013, starting all 13 games. Kouandjio returned as a starter his senior year in 2014.<ref name="s200">{{cite web | last=Kirkpatrick | first=Cliff | title=Tide’s Kouandjio a pleasant surprise on offensive line | website=Montgomery Advertiser | date=2014-10-31 | url=https://www.montgomeryadvertiser.com/story/sports/college/alabama/2014/10/31/tides-kouandjio-pleasant-surprise-offensive-line/18227075/ | access-date=2024-10-03}}</ref> He started all 14 games and was named a second-team [[All-American]].

===Washington Redskins (first stint)===
The [[Washington Redskins]] selected Kouandjio in the fourth round with the 112th overall pick in the [[2015 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Czarda |first=Stephen |date=May 2, 2015 |title=Redskins Pick Arie Kouandjio In Fourth Round |url=http://www.redskins.com/news-and-events/article-1/Redskins-Pick-Arie-Kouandjio-In-Fourth-Round-/ae7ac56b-8b43-4d4d-8948-580323a5a080 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150505004800/http://www.redskins.com/news-and-events/article-1/Redskins-Pick-Arie-Kouandjio-In-Fourth-Round-/ae7ac56b-8b43-4d4d-8948-580323a5a080 |archive-date=May 5, 2015 |access-date=May 3, 2015 |website=Redskins.com}}</ref> He signed a four-year contract on May 11, 2015.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 11, 2015 |title=Nine Redskins Draft Picks Agree To Terms |url=http://www.redskins.com/news-and-events/article-1/Nine-Redskins-Draft-Picks-Agree-To-Terms/107e54e5-dde6-488a-885a-8824cc641bcc |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170910040806/http://www.redskins.com/news-and-events/article-1/Nine-Redskins-Draft-Picks-Agree-To-Terms/107e54e5-dde6-488a-885a-8824cc641bcc |archive-date=September 10, 2017 |access-date=May 21, 2015 |website=Redskins.com}}</ref>

On September 2, 2017, Kouandjio was waived by the Redskins.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 2, 2017 |title=9/2: Redskins Make Roster Moves |url=http://www.redskins.com/news/article-1/92-Redskins-Make-Roster-Moves/ec94fade-58e8-4d11-a499-b8317f337ae0 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170905031831/http://www.redskins.com/news/article-1/92-Redskins-Make-Roster-Moves/ec94fade-58e8-4d11-a499-b8317f337ae0 |archive-date=September 5, 2017 |website=Redskins.com}}</ref>

===Baltimore Ravens===
On September 19, 2017, Kouandjio was signed to the [[practice squad]] of the [[Baltimore Ravens]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mink, Ryan |date=September 19, 2017 |title=Ravens Sign Two Offensive Linemen to 53-Man Roster |url=http://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/article-1/Ravens-Sign-Two-Offensive-Linemen-to-53-Man-Roster/6fe0ab81-3e84-417e-94ba-589bc499d448 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171023105658/http://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/article-1/Ravens-Sign-Two-Offensive-Linemen-to-53-Man-Roster/6fe0ab81-3e84-417e-94ba-589bc499d448 |archive-date=October 23, 2017 |website=BaltimoreRavens.com}}</ref>

===Washington Redskins (second stint)===
On October 28, 2017, Kouandjio was signed by the Redskins off the Ravens' practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Czarda, Stephen |date=October 28, 2017 |title=Redskins Sign Arie Kouandjio And Orlando Franklin |url=http://www.redskins.com/news/article-1/Redskins-Sign-Arie-Kouandjio-And-Orlando-Franklin/44015d4a-9122-4a3f-a0d1-47aba0e61110 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171101190724/http://www.redskins.com/news/article-1/Redskins-Sign-Arie-Kouandjio-And-Orlando-Franklin/44015d4a-9122-4a3f-a0d1-47aba0e61110 |archive-date=November 1, 2017 |website=Redskins.com}}</ref> He played in eight games in 2017, starting six at right guard.

On May 15, 2018, it was announced that Kouandjio would undergo quad surgery for a partial tear.<ref name="b702">{{cite web | last=Patra | first=Kevin | title=Redskins G Arie Kouandjio to undergo quad surgery | website=NFL.com | date=2018-05-15 | url=https://www.nfl.com/news/redskins-g-arie-kouandjio-to-undergo-quad-surgery-0ap3000000932901 | access-date=2024-10-03}}</ref> The next week, following the surgery, it was reported that Kouandjio would miss the entire 2018 season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Williams, Charean |date=May 21, 2018 |title=Report: Arie Kouandjio will miss season after surgery |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2018/05/21/report-arie-kouandjio-will-miss-season-after-surgery/ |website=ProFootballTalk.NBCSports.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Czarda |first=Stephen |title=Redskins Sign Guard Isaiah Williams |url=https://www.redskins.com/news/redskins-sign-guard-isaiah-williams |access-date=May 22, 2018 |website=Redskins.com}}</ref>

===New York Guardians===
Kouandjio was selected by the [[New York Guardians]] of the [[XFL (2020)|XFL]] in the 10th round in phase two in the [[2020 XFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=October 15, 2019 |title=OFFENSIVE LINEMEN DRAFT TRACKER |work=XFL.com |url=https://www.xfl.com/en-US/articles/phase-2-offensive-line-draft-tracker |access-date=October 16, 2019}}</ref>

Kouandjio's younger brother, [[Cyrus Kouandjio|Cyrus]], who played at Alabama as an offensive tackle and was selected in second round of the [[2014 NFL draft]] by the [[Buffalo Bills]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 14, 2013 |title=Alabama Crimson Tide linemen Cyrus and Arie Kouandjio just 'regular kids' |url=http://www.sportingnews.com/ncaa-football/story/2013-04-10/alabama-crimson-tide-spring-football-depth-chart-cyrus-arie-kouandjio-nick-saban |access-date=December 3, 2014 |archive-date=May 26, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150526002727/http://www.sportingnews.com/ncaa-football/story/2013-04-10/alabama-crimson-tide-spring-football-depth-chart-cyrus-arie-kouandjio-nick-saban |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Czarda |first=Stephen |date=May 2, 2015 |title=Arie Kouandjio Spends Draft Weekend With His Brother, A Bills Guard |url=http://www.redskins.com/news-and-events/blog/article-1/Arie-Kouandjio-Spends-Draft-Weekend-With-His-Brother-A-Bills-Guard/164719e2-d054-460a-ab40-5ab7beed94f3 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150505020954/http://www.redskins.com/news-and-events/blog/article-1/Arie-Kouandjio-Spends-Draft-Weekend-With-His-Brother-A-Bills-Guard/164719e2-d054-460a-ab40-5ab7beed94f3 |archive-date=May 5, 2015 |access-date=May 3, 2015 |website=Redskins.com}}</ref> Kouandjio became a US citizen on September 13, 2016.<ref name=ArieCitizenship/>

Winston]] during the 31–17 road victory.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401128010 |title=Sherman, 49ers upend Winston, Buccaneers 31-7 |agency=Associated Press|date=September 8, pass |date=September 22, 2019 |agency=Associated Press |website=ESPN.com |access-date=April 1, 2020}} During Week 6 against the Rams, Armstead recorded a season high 6 tackles, half a sack on [[Jared Goff]], and recovered a fumble lost by Goff during the 20–7 road victory.{{Cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401128128 |title=49ers remain unbeaten with 20-7 win over slumping Rams |date=October 13, 2019 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=April 1, 2020 |agency=Associated Press}} In the next game against the [[Washington Redskins]], he sacked [[Case Keenum]] once during the 9–0 road victory. With that sack, Armstead set a new single season career high of 3.5 sacks.{{cite web |date=October 20, 2019 |title=49ers beat Redskins in ugly 9-0 game to improve to 6-0 |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401127977 |access-date=April 1, 2020 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press}} The following week against the [[Carolina Panthers]], Armstead sacked [[Kyle Allen (American football)|Kyle Allen]] twice during the 51–13 win.{{cite web |date=October 27, 2019 |title=Coleman's 4 TDs lead 49ers past Panthers 51-13 |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401128050 |access-date=April 1, 2020 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press}} Two weeks later against the Seahawks on ''[[Monday Night Football]]'', he sacked [[Russell Wilson]] 1.5 times during the 27–24 overtime loss.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401127992 |title=Seahawks knock 49ers from unbeaten ranks with 27-24 OT win |date=November 11, 2019 |agency=Associated Press |website=ESPN.com |access-date=April 1, 2020}} During Week 12 against the [[Green Bay Packers]] on ''[[NBC Sunday Night Football|Sunday Night Football]]'', Armstead sacked [[Aaron Rodgers]] twice during the 37–8 win.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401128004 |title=49ers start 3-game gauntlet with 37-8 win over Packers |date=November 24, 2019 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press |access-date=April 1, 2020}} The 2019 season was a breakout season for Armstead. He also ranked second on the 49ers regarding tackles for loss.{{Cite web |title=Arik Armstead 2019 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/A/ArmsAr01/gamelog/2019/ |access-date=April 1, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}} Armstead made his playoff debut in the [[National Football Conference]] (NFC) Divisional Round of the playoffs against the Vikings. During the game, Armstead sacked [[Kirk Cousins]] once in the 27–10 win.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401131040 |title=49ers win 1st playoff game in 6 years, 27-10 over Vikings |date=January 11, 2020 |agency=Associated Press |website=ESPN.com |access-date=April 1, 2020}} In the NFC Championship Game against the Packers, he sacked Aaron Rodgers once during the 37–20 win.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401131045 |title=Mostert lifts 49ers to Super Bowl with 37-20 win vs Packers |date=January 19, 2020|agency=Associated Press |website=ESPN.com |access-date=January 19, 2020}} In [[Super Bowl LIV]] against the Chiefs, Armstead recorded three tackles during the 31–20 loss.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401131047 |title=Mahomes leads Chiefs' rally past 49ers in Super Bowl, 31-20 |date=February 2, 2020|agency=Associated Press |website=ESPN.com |access-date=April 1, 2020}} ====2020 season==== On March 16, 2020, Armstead signed a five-year, $85 million contract extension with the 49ers with $48.5 million guaranteed.{{cite news |title=49ers Sign DL Arik Armstead to Five-year Extension |url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-sign-arik-armstead-to-five-year-extension |website=49ers.com |date=March 16, 2020 |access-date=March 16, 2020}}{{cite web|title=Arik Armstead, 49ers agree to 5-year mega contract|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/arik-armstead-49ers-agree-to-5-year-mega-contract-0ap3000001106413|author=Patra, Kevin|website=NFL.com|date=March 16, 2020}} During Week 2 against the [[New York Jets]], he recorded his first sack of the season on [[Sam Darnold]] during the 31–13 road victory.{{Cite web |title=San Francisco 49ers at New York Jets - September 20th, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202009200nyj.htm |access-date=September 22, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}} He was placed on the reserve/[[COVID-19]] list by the team on November 16, 2020,{{cite news |title=49ers Place DL Arik Armstead on Reserve/COVID-19 List |url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-place-dl-arik-armstead-on-reserve-covid-19-list |website=49ers.com |date=November 16, 2020 |access-date=December 23, 2020}} and activated on November 25.{{cite news |author=Madson, Kyle |title=49ers remove 2 players from COVID-19 list ahead of Week 12 game vs. Rams |url=https://ninerswire.usatoday.com/2020/11/25/49ers-remove-2-players-from-covid-19-list-ahead-of-week-12-game-vs-rams/ |website=USAToday.com |date=November 25, 2020 |access-date=December 23, 2020}} In the 2020 season, he started in all 16 games. He finished with 3.5 sacks, 49 total tackles, and three passes defended.{{Cite web |title=Arik Armstead 2020 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/A/ArmsAr01/gamelog/2020/ |access-date=February 19, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}} ====2021 season==== On December 7, 2021, Armstead was nominated by the 49ers for the [[Walter Payton NFL Man of the Year Award]].{{Cite news |date=December 7, 2021 |title=Arik Armstead Named 49ers Nominee for Walter Payton NFL Man of the Year |url=https://www.49ers.com/news/arik-armstead-named-49ers-nominee-for-walter-payton-nfl-man-of-the-year |access-date=February 18, 2024 |work=49ers.com}} During Week 18, in the 49ers final game of the regular season, Armstead recorded 2.5 sacks in a 27–24 overtime victory against the Rams.{{Cite web |title=San Francisco 49ers at Los Angeles Rams - January 9th, 2022 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202201090ram.htm |access-date=December 6, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}} The victory clinched the 49ers' spot in the [[2021–22 NFL playoffs|playoffs]] that year. In the 2021 season, Armstead started in all 17 games.{{Cite web |title=Arik Armstead 2021 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/A/ArmsAr01/gamelog/2021/ |access-date=February 19, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}} He had six sacks and 63 total tackles. Two weeks later, in the [[2021–22 NFL playoffs#NFC: San Francisco 49ers 13, Green Bay Packers 10|NFC Divisional Round]], Armstead sacked Packers quarterback [[Aaron Rodgers]] twice in a 13-10 victory that sent the 49ers to the [[2021–22 NFL playoffs#NFC: Los Angeles Rams 20, San Francisco 49ers 17|NFC Championship Game]].{{cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/A/ArmsAr01/gamelog/2021/ |title=Arik Armstead 2021 Game Log |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |access-date=December 6, 2022}} ====2022 season==== On November 10, 2022, Armstead revealed that he was rehabbing a [[stress fracture|hairline fracture]] in his left ankle.{{Cite web |last=Branch |first=Eric |date=November 9, 2022 |title=49ers' Arik Armstead has hairline fracture; Mike McGlinchey jokes about '18 draft |url=https://www.sfchronicle.com/sports/49ers/article/49ers-Armstead-has-hairline-fracture-17572821.php |access-date=June 30, 2023 |website=San Francisco Chronicle |language=en}} He appeared in and started nine games. He recorded two sacks in the 49ers' three postseason games.{{Cite web |title=Arik Armstead 2022 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/A/ArmsAr01/gamelog/2022/ |access-date=February 19, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}} ====2023 season==== In the 2023 season, Armstead appeared in and started 12 games. He finished with five sacks and 27 total tackles.{{Cite web |title=Arik Armstead 2023 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/A/ArmsAr01/gamelog/2023/ |access-date=February 18, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}} In [[Super Bowl LVIII]], Armstead recorded one sack and six total tackles in the 25–22 overtime loss to the Chiefs.{{Cite web |title=Super Bowl LVIII - San Francisco 49ers vs. Kansas City Chiefs - February 11th, 2024 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202402110kan.htm |access-date=February 18, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}} Two days after losing the Super Bowl, it was revealed that Armstead was playing through a knee injury during the playoffs, which later turned out to be a torn meniscus. Armstead told reporters that he suffered the injury on December 3, 2023, after a game against the [[Philadelphia Eagles]]. Armstead required surgery on the meniscus, which caused him to miss most off-season activities.{{Cite web |last=Edholm |first=Eric |date=February 13, 2024 |title=Arik Armstead says he played through postseason with torn meniscus, will undergo surgery|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/niners-dl-arik-armstead-says-he-played-through-postseason-with-torn-meniscus-will-undergo-surgery |access-date=February 13, 2024 |website=NFL.com}} On March 13, 2024, Armstead was released by the 49ers.{{cite web|title=49ers Release Arik Armstead, Re-Sign Quarterback and Other Moves|url=https://www.49ers.com/news/free-agency-arik-armstead-colton-mckivitz-george-odum-brandon-allen-quarterback-dl|website=49ers.com|date=March 13, 2024|access-date=March 13, 2024}} ===Jacksonville Jaguars=== On March 15, 2024, the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] signed Armstead to a three-year, $51 million contract.{{Cite web |last=Oehser |first=John |date=15 March 2024 |title=Defensive Lineman Arik Armstead Signs Deal with Jaguars |url=https://www.jaguars.com/news/defensive-lineman-arik-armstead-signs-deal-with-jaguars-2024 |access-date=15 March 2024 |website=Jaguars.com |publisher=Jacksonville Jaguars}} He had two sacks, 29 tackles, and three passes defended.{{Cite web |title=Arik Armstead 2024 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/A/ArmsAr01/gamelog/2024/ |access-date=2026-04-19 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}} In the 2025 season, he had 5.5 sacks and 28 tackles.{{Cite web |title=Arik Armstead 2025 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/A/ArmsAr01/gamelog/2025/ |access-date=2026-04-19 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}} ==NFL career statistics== === Regular season === {|class="wikitable" style="text-align:center;" |- ! rowspan="2"| Year ! rowspan="2"| Team ! colspan="2"| Games ! colspan="5"| Tackles ! colspan="4"| Fumbles ! colspan="6"| Interceptions |- ! '''Arden Key Jr.''' (born May 3, 1996) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[linebacker]] for the [[Indianapolis Colts]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[LSU Tigers football|LSU Tigers]], and was selected by the [[Oakland Raiders]] in the third round of the [[2018 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Key attended [[Hapeville Charter Career Academy]] in [[Union City, Georgia]]. He recorded 15.5 [[qb sack|sacks]] as a senior, eight as a junior and 12 as a sophomore. He committed to [[Louisiana State University]] (LSU) to play [[college football]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theadvocate.com/baton_rouge/sports/lsu/article_c50665fd-aa38-5436-b59c-b7bf0b96aeee.html|title=Four star Georgia defensive end Arden Key commits to LSU|author=Dellenger, Ross|work=The Advocate|date=April 23, 2016|access-date=April 3, 2018|archive-date=April 4, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180404200806/http://www.theadvocate.com/baton_rouge/sports/lsu/article_c50665fd-aa38-5436-b59c-b7bf0b96aeee.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.thestate.com/sports/college/university-of-south-carolina/usc-recruiting/article18201092.html|title='A lifetime decision': Arden Key picks LSU over the Gamecocks|author=Kendall, Josh|date=February 3, 2015|access-date=April 3, 2018|archive-date=April 3, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180403234728/http://www.thestate.com/sports/college/university-of-south-carolina/usc-recruiting/article18201092.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

Regarded as a four-star recruit by [[ESPN]], Key was ranked as the No. 6 [[defensive end]] prospect in the class of 2015.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.espn.com/college-sports/football/recruiting/player/_/id/171517/arden-key |work=ESPN |title=Arden Key Recruiting Profile |access-date=November 13, 2016 |archive-date=November 14, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161114005331/http://www.espn.com/college-sports/football/recruiting/player/_/id/171517/arden-key |url-status=live }}</ref>

==College career==
As a [[true freshman]] at LSU in 2015, Key played in 12 games and started the final nine. He recorded 41 [[tackle move|tackles]] and five sacks and was named a freshman [[All-American]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.espn.com/blog/sec/post/_/id/119793/twenty-sacks-or-not-arden-key-will-be-a-weapon-for-lsus-defense |title=Twenty sacks or not, Arden Key will be a weapon for LSU's defense |access-date=October 2, 2016 |archive-date=October 3, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161003054159/http://www.espn.com/blog/sec/post/_/id/119793/twenty-sacks-or-not-arden-key-will-be-a-weapon-for-lsus-defense |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.theadvertiser.com/story/sports/2016/08/23/lsu-olb-arden-key-enjoying-new-defense/89200676/ |title=LSU OLB Arden Key enjoying new defense |access-date=October 2, 2016 |archive-date=September 14, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170914040352/http://www.theadvertiser.com/story/sports/2016/08/23/lsu-olb-arden-key-enjoying-new-defense/89200676/ |url-status=live }}</ref> As a sophomore in 2016, he set a single-season school record by recording 12 sacks.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Lopez|first1=Andrew|title=Arden Key breaks LSU single-season sack record|url=http://www.nola.com/lsu/index.ssf/2016/12/arden_key_breaks_lsu_single-se.html|access-date=September 13, 2017|work=The Times-Picayune|date=December 31, 2016|archive-date=September 14, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170914034447/http://www.nola.com/lsu/index.ssf/2016/12/arden_key_breaks_lsu_single-se.html|url-status=live}}</ref> He earned first-team [[List of All-SEC football teams|All-Southeastern Conference]] honors from the [[Associated Press]].<ref>{{cite news|title=It's a Sweep: No 1. Alabama Cleans up on AP All-SEC Team|url=https://abcnews.go.com/Sports/wireStory/sweep-alabama-cleans-ap-sec-team-44064709|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161209034416/https://abcnews.go.com/Sports/wireStory/sweep-alabama-cleans-ap-sec-team-44064709|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 9, 2016|access-date=December 10, 2016|agency=Associated Press|work=ABC News|date=December 8, 2016}}</ref> As a junior in 2017, Key was limited to 8 games due to injury, but finished with 33 tackles, 4 sacks, and a forced fumble. On January 4, 2018, Key officially announced that he would be entering the [[2018 NFL draft]].<ref>{{cite web|title=LSU DE Arden Key entering the draft|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/lsu-standout-arden-key-intends-to-enter-2018-nfl-draft-0ap3000000902673|publisher=NFL|date=January 4, 2018|access-date=April 7, 2022}}</ref>

Prior to Key's junior season, he was projected as the number one overall prospect for the 2018 NFL Draft by Chris Trapasso of [[CBS Sports]].<ref>{{cite web|title=An incredibly early look at the top 100 prospects in the 2018 NFL Draft: 1-20|first=Chris|last=Trapasso|work=CBS Sports|date=June 1, 2017|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/draft/news/an-incredibly-early-look-at-the-top-100-prospects-in-the-2018-nfl-draft-1-20|access-date=September 2, 2017|archive-date=September 3, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170903031216/https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/draft/news/an-incredibly-early-look-at-the-top-100-prospects-in-the-2018-nfl-draft-1-20/|url-status=live}}</ref> In January 2018, he was ranked as the number two draft prospect at the outside linebacker position, behind [[Tremaine Edmunds]] of [[Virginia Tech Hokies football|Virginia Tech]], by [[Mel Kiper]] of [[ESPN]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://abcnews.go.com/Sports/mel-kipers-top-10-prospects-position-2018-nfl/story?id=52263598|title=Mel Kiper's top 10 prospects at each position for 2018 NFL draft|website=ABC News|date=January 10, 2018|access-date=January 10, 2018|archive-date=March 15, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230315074206/https://abcnews.go.com/Sports/mel-kipers-top-10-prospects-position-2018-nfl/story?id=52263598|url-status=live}}</ref> Key was projected to be an early first round selection, but his off-the-field issues caused his draft stock to plummet.

===Oakland / Las Vegas Raiders===
Key was selected by the [[Oakland Raiders]] in the third round as the 87th pick overall.<ref>{{cite web|title=Arden Key selected by Oakland Raiders in 2018 Draft|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/raiders-end-draft-wait-for-lsu-s-arden-key-0ap3000000928051|publisher=NFL|date=April 27, 2018|access-date=April 7, 2022|archive-date=January 25, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220125001025/https://www.nfl.com/news/raiders-end-draft-wait-for-lsu-s-arden-key-0ap3000000928051|url-status=live}}</ref> He played all 16 games during the [[2018 Oakland Raiders season|2018 season]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Arden Key 2018 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/K/KeyxAr00/gamelog/2018/ |access-date=2024-12-11 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

Key played seven games in the [[2019 Oakland Raiders season|2019 season]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Arden Key 2019 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/K/KeyxAr00/gamelog/2019/ |access-date=2024-12-11 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> After having two sacks in his final two games, Key suffered a broken foot and was ruled out the rest of the season. He was placed on injured reserve on November 7, 2019.<ref>{{cite web|title=Raiders promote linebacker Quentin Poling and place defensive end Arden Key on IR|url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-promote-linebacker-quentin-poling-and-place-defensive-end-arden-key-on-i|website=Raiders.com|date=November 7, 2019|access-date=November 9, 2019|archive-date=November 9, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191109162901/https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-promote-linebacker-quentin-poling-and-place-defensive-end-arden-key-on-i|url-status=live}}</ref>

Key played 14 games during the [[2020 Las Vegas Raiders season|2020 season]], missing two games due to illness.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Arden Key 2020 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/K/KeyxAr00/gamelog/2020/ |access-date=2024-12-11 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He was placed on the reserve/[[COVID-19]] list by the team on November 18, 2020,<ref>{{cite news |title=Raiders Add 7 Players To COVID-19 List Ahead Of Rematch Vs. Chiefs |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/losangeles/news/raiders-7-players-covid-19-list-ferrell-joyner-abram-collins-hankins-irving-johnson-key-vickers/ |website=CBS News Los Angeles |date=November 18, 2020 |access-date=April 7, 2022 |archive-date=April 7, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220407200223/https://www.cbsnews.com/losangeles/news/raiders-7-players-covid-19-list-ferrell-joyner-abram-collins-hankins-irving-johnson-key-vickers/ |url-status=live }}</ref> and activated three days later.<ref>{{cite news |author=Gutierrez, Paul |title=Las Vegas Raiders activate 7 off reserve/COVID-19 list |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/30360175/source-las-vegas-raiders-activate-7-reserve-covid-19-list |website=ESPN |date=November 21, 2020 |access-date=December 25, 2020 |archive-date=January 5, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210105022005/https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/30360175/source-las-vegas-raiders-activate-7-reserve-covid-19-list |url-status=live }}</ref> On December 26, 2020, in a Week 16 home game against the [[Miami Dolphins]], Key committed a 15-yard personal foul penalty when he grabbed the facemask of Dolphin QB [[Ryan Fitzpatrick]] on a play where the Dolphins gained 34 yards; the penalty and catch put Miami in [[field goal]] range and Miami hit one from 44 yards to earn a 26-25 win, which eliminated the Raiders from playoff contention.

Key was waived on April 15, 2021.<ref>{{cite news |author=Alper, Josh |title=Raiders waive Maurice Hurst and Arden Key; release Kyle Sloter |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2021/04/15/raiders-waive-maurice-hurst-and-arden-key-release-kyle-sloter/ |website=ProFootballTalk |publisher=NBC Sports |date=April 15, 2021 |access-date=April 15, 2021 |archive-date=April 15, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210415202754/https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2021/04/15/raiders-waive-maurice-hurst-and-arden-key-release-kyle-sloter/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

===San Francisco 49ers===
On April 23, 2021, Key signed a one-year contract with the [[San Francisco 49ers]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=49ers Sign Two Defensive Linemen to One-year Deals|url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-sign-two-defensive-linemen-to-one-year-deals|publisher=San Francisco 49ers|date=April 23, 2021|access-date=April 23, 2021|archive-date=April 23, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210423204005/https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-sign-two-defensive-linemen-to-one-year-deals|url-status=live}}</ref> He played all 17 games of the [[2021 San Francisco 49ers season|2021 season]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Arden Key 2021 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/K/KeyxAr00/gamelog/2021/ |access-date=2024-12-11 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

=== Jacksonville Jaguars ===
On March 30, 2022, Key signed a one-year contract with the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Alper |first=Josh |date=2022-03-30 |title=Jaguars sign Arden Key |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2022/03/30/jaguars-sign-arden-key/ |access-date=2022-03-30 |website=ProFootballTalk |publisher=NBC Sports |archive-date=March 31, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220331130457/https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2022/03/30/jaguars-sign-arden-key/ |url-status=live }}</ref> He played in all 17 games with three starts, recording 27 tackles and 4.5 sacks.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Arden Key 2022 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/K/KeyxAr00/gamelog/2022/ |access-date=2024-12-11 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===Tennessee Titans===
[[file:Arden Key Titans vs Patriots NOV2024.png|thumb|right|250px|Key playing for the Titans in 2024.]]
On March 20, 2023, Key signed a three-year, $21 million contract with the [[Tennessee Titans]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Titans Agree to Terms With Former Jaguars Defensive Lineman Arden Key|url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-agree-to-terms-with-former-jaguars-defensive-lineman-arden-key|author=Wyatt, Jim|website=TennesseeTitans.com|date=March 20, 2023}}</ref> He played in 17 games with nine starts during the [[2023 Tennessee Titans season|2023 season]], recording 30 tackles, six sacks, and two forced fumbles.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Arden Key 2023 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/K/KeyxAr00/gamelog/2023/ |access-date=2024-12-11 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

On July 30, 2024, Key was suspended 6 games for violating the NFL's policy against performance–enhancing drugs.<ref name="h330">{{cite web | last=Davenport | first=Turron | title=Source: Titans LB Key facing 6-game PED ban | website=ESPN.com | date=2024-07-30 | url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/40681959/titans-lb-arden-key-facing-six-game-suspension-source-says | access-date=2025-02-17}}</ref> However, Key successfully appealed the ban, and his suspension was overturned on August 17.<ref name="j152">{{cite web | last=Davenport | first=Turron | title=Source: Titans' Key has 6-game ban overturned | website=ESPN.com | date=2024-08-17 | url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/40895006/suspension-overturned-titans-lb-arden-key-source-says | access-date=2025-02-17}}</ref> He played 16 games during the [[2024 Tennessee Titans season|2024 season]], only missing the last game due to injury. He finished with a career high of 42 tackles, 6.5 sacks, 18 pressures, and a pass deflection.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Arden Key 2024 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/K/KeyxAr00/gamelog/2024/ |access-date=2025-02-17 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

===Indianapolis Colts===
On March 12, 2026, Key signed with the [[Indianapolis Colts]] on a two-year, $20 million contract with $11 million guaranteed.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Foster |first1=Amanda |title=Colts sign free agent DE Arden Key |url=https://www.colts.com/news/colts-sign-free-agent-de-arden-key |website=Colts.com |access-date=13 March 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/colts-to-add-arden-key-on-two-year-deal|title=Colts to add Arden Key on two-year deal|first=Josh|last=Alper|date=March 9, 2026|work=NBCSports.com}}</ref>
