'''Armani Watts''' (born March 19, 1996) is an American professional [[gridiron football|football]] [[defensive back]]. He played [[college football]] at [[Texas A&M Aggies football|Texas A&M]] and was selected by the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] in the fourth round of the [[2018 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 27, 2018 |title=Former Texas A&M safety Armani Watts to compete in Senior Bowl today |url=http://www.theeagle.com/aggie_sports/former-texas-a-m-safety-armani-watts-to-compete-in/article_959cbf66-0329-11e8-a63f-d3bdf9b5cf37.html |access-date=October 18, 2018 |website=The Eagle |language=en}}</ref>

==Early life==
Watts attended and played [[high school football]] at [[North Forney High School]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Richards |first=Mathew |title=North Forney grad, Armani Watts, snags two interceptions for Kansas City Chiefs against Green Bay Packers |language=en |work=inForney.com |url=https://www.inforney.com/sports/north-forney-grad-armani-watts-snags-two-interceptions-for-kansas/article_5c85039e-b52d-11e8-9903-9bc5988fb082.html |access-date=October 18, 2018}}</ref>

==College career==
Watts attended and played [[college football]] at Texas A&M from 2014 to 2017 under head coach [[Kevin Sumlin]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Baby |first=Ben |date=July 12, 2017 |title=Texas A&M's Christian Kirk, Armani Watts are playing for Kevin Sumlin as coach sits on the hot seat |url=https://sportsday.dallasnews.com/college-sports/collegesports/2017/07/12/texas-ams-christian-kirkarmani-watts-playing-kevin-sumlin-coach-sits-hot-seat |access-date=October 18, 2018 |website=SportsDay |language=en}}</ref> He was a four-year starter for the Aggies and led the team in [[interceptions]] as a freshman.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2014 Texas A&M Aggies Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/texas-am/2014.html |access-date=October 18, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In 2017, he started 12 games, had 87 [[tackled gridiron|tackles]], 10 for loss, four interceptions, five pass breakups, two [[fumble]] recoveries and two blocked kicks.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Armani Watts 2017 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/armani-watts-1/gamelog/2017/ |access-date=October 18, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Watts was an [[List of All-SEC football teams|All-Southeastern Conference]] selection and third-team [[All-America]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Perroni |first=Brian |date=December 4, 2017 |title=Texas A&M players make AP All-SEC teams |url=https://247sports.com/college/texas-am/article/texas-am-players-make-ap-all-sec-teams-christian-kirk-armani-watts-111731329/ |access-date=October 18, 2018 |website=247 Sports |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== Minnesota Vikings===
Watts was selected by the [[Minnesota Vikings]] in the sixth round (190th overall) of the [[2019 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gates |first=Christopher |date=April 27, 2019 |title=2019 NFL Draft Results: Minnesota Vikings select Armon Watts |url=https://www.dailynorseman.com/2019/4/27/18518707/2019-nfl-draft-results-minnesota-vikings-armon-watts-arkansas-razorbacks |access-date=April 27, 2019 |website=Daily Norseman}}</ref>

On November 10, 2019, Watts combined for a sack of [[Dallas Cowboys]] quarterback [[Dak Prescott]] with teammate [[Everson Griffen]] in a 28–24 win on ''[[NBC Sunday Night Football|Sunday Night Football]]''. It was his first career game. He was placed on [[injured reserve]] on December 31, 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 31, 2019 |title=Vikings Sign Bills DE Eddie Yarbrough to 53-Man Roster, Place DT Armon Watts on IR |url=https://www.vikings.com/news/vikings-sign-bills-de-eddie-yarbrough-to-53-man-roster-place-dt-armon-watts-on-i |website=Vikings.com}}</ref>

Watts was placed on the reserve/[[COVID-19]] list by the Vikings on August 4, 2020,<ref>{{Cite news |date=August 4, 2020 |title=Vikings Announce Roster Moves; Justin Jefferson Activated |work=Vikings.com |url=https://www.vikings.com/news/justin-jefferson-covid-19-activated-pj-hall-reverts-roster-moves |access-date=August 4, 2020}}</ref> and was activated two days later.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Alper, Josh |date=August 6, 2020 |title=Vikings activate Armon Watts, waive Bralon Addison |work=NBCSports.com |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2020/08/06/vikings-activate-armon-watts-waive-bralon-addison/ |access-date=August 10, 2020}}</ref>

Watts was waived by the Vikings on August 30, 2022.<ref>{{Cite news |date=August 30, 2022 |title=Vikings Announce Roster Moves, Set Initial 53-Man Roster |work=Vikings.com |url=https://www.vikings.com/news/roster-moves-initial-53-man-waived-injured-2022}}</ref>

===Chicago Bears===
On August 31, 2022, Watts was claimed by waivers by the [[Chicago Bears]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mayer |first=Larry |date=August 31, 2022 |title=Roster Moves: Bears claim six players off waivers |url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/roster-moves-bears-claim-six-players-off-waivers-alex-leatherwood-alabama |access-date=January 29, 2023 |website=ChicagoBears.com}}</ref>

===Pittsburgh Steelers===
On April 12, 2023, Watts signed with the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Varley |first=Teresa |date=April 12, 2023 |title=Watts signed to one-year contract |url=https://www.steelers.com/news/watts-signed-to-one-year-contract |access-date=May 18, 2023 |website=Steelers.com}}</ref>

===New England Patriots===
On March 15, 2024, Watts signed with the [[New England Patriots]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Patriots Announce Four Signings|url=https://www.patriots.com/news/patriots-announce-four-signings|website=Patriots.com|date=March 15, 2024}}</ref> He was placed on injured reserve on August 27.<ref>{{cite web|title=Patriots Make Roster Moves to Reach the 53-Man Roster Limit|url=https://www.patriots.com/news/patriots-release-16-players-place-three-players-on-injured-reserve|website=Patriots.com|date=August 27, 2024}}</ref> He was released with an Injury Settlement on October 2, 2024.

===New York Giants===
On October 15, 2024, Watts signed with the [[New York Giants]] practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Salomone |first=Dan |date=October 15, 2024 |title=Giants sign DT Armon Watts to practice squad; CB Duke Shelley released |url=https://www.giants.com/news/armon-watts-defensive-tackle-vikings-bears-steelers-patriots-arkansas-duke-shelley-cornerback |access-date=16 October 2024 |website=Giants.com}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on October 22.<ref name="l150">{{cite web | last=Eisen | first=Michael | title=Giants sign DT Armon Watts off practice squad; OLB Boogie Basham waived | website=Giants.com| date=2024-10-22 | url=https://www.giants.com/news/giants-sign-dt-armon-watts-off-practice-squad-olb-boogie-basham-waived | access-date=2024-11-21}}</ref> On January 3, 2024, Watts was placed on injured reserve with a knee injury.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 3, 2024 |title=Giants' Armon Watts: Shifts to IR|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/giants-armon-watts-shifts-to-ir/|website=cbssports.com}}</ref>

'''Arlington Hambright''' (born January 30, 1996) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Guard (gridiron football)|guard]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL).<ref>{{cite web | url=https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2020/4/25/21236454/2020-nfl-draft-bears-pick-colorado-g-arlington-hambright-in-7th-round | title=NFL Draft: Bears pick Colorado OL Arlington Hambright in 7th round | date=April 25, 2020 }}</ref> He played [[college football]] for the [[Colorado Buffaloes football|Colorado Buffaloes]]. He was a member of the [[Chicago Bears]], [[New England Patriots]], [[Indianapolis Colts]], [[Houston Texans]], [[Tennessee Titans]], and [[Montreal Alouettes]].

After graduating [[Belleville High School (Michigan)|Belleville]] as a no-star recruit, Hambright played his first two years of college football at [[Garden City Community College]]. He then transferred to [[Oklahoma State Cowboys football|Oklahoma State]], where he redshirted a year and had a year cut short due to injury. Hambright played his final season of college at [[Colorado Buffaloes football|Colorado]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Brugler |first=Dane |url=https://cdn.theathletic.com/app/uploads/2020/04/21144256/2020-NFL-DRAFT-FINAL-2.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200504081443/https://cdn.theathletic.com/app/uploads/2020/04/21144256/2020-NFL-DRAFT-FINAL-2.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-date=May 4, 2020 |title=The Athletic's 2020 NFL Draft Guide |date=April 7, 2020 |publisher=The Athletic |page=102 |access-date=April 27, 2020}}</ref>

Hambright was selected by the [[Chicago Bears]] in the seventh round (226th overall) of the [[2020 NFL draft]], previously acquired from the [[Las Vegas Raiders]] as part of the blockbuster [[Khalil Mack]] trade that sent two first round picks ([[Josh Jacobs]] and [[Damon Arnette]]) to the Raiders.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lieser |first=Jason |date=April 25, 2020 |title=NFL Draft: Bears pick Colorado OL Arlington Hambright in 7th round |url=https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2020/4/25/21236454/2020-nfl-draft-bears-pick-colorado-g-arlington-hambright-in-7th-round |access-date=April 27, 2020 |website=Chicago Sun-Times}}</ref> He signed a four-year rookie contract with the team on July 21.<ref>{{cite news|last=Mayer|first=Larry|url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/bears-sign-all-seven-of-their-2020-draft-picks|title=Bears sign all seven of their 2020 draft picks|publisher=[[Chicago Bears]]|date=July 21, 2020|access-date=July 21, 2020}}</ref> Hambright made his NFL debut on special teams against the [[New Orleans Saints]] in Week 8, and made his first NFL start the following week against the [[Tennessee Titans]]. He appeared in nine games during the [[2020 Chicago Bears season|2020 season]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Arlington Hambright 2020 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/H/HambAr00/gamelog/2020/ |access-date=2025-01-06 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

On August 31, 2021, Hambright was waived by the Bears and re-signed to the [[practice squad]] the next day.<ref>{{cite web|title=Roster Moves: Bears announce 53-man roster|url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/roster-moves-bears-announce-53-man-roster|author=Mayer, Larry|website=ChicagoBears.com|date=August 31, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Roster Moves: Bears sign 13 players to practice squad|url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/roster-moves-bears-sign-13-players-to-practice-squad|author=Mayer, Larry|website=ChicagoBears.com|date=September 1, 2021}}</ref>

===New England Patriots===
On January 18, 2022, Hambright signed a reserve/future contract with the [[New England Patriots]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Patriots sign offensive lineman Arlington Hambright to a future contract|url=https://www.patriots.com/news/patriots-sign-offensive-lineman-arlington-hambright-to-a-future-contract|website=Patriots.com|date=January 18, 2022}}</ref> He was waived on August 30.<ref>{{cite web|title=Patriots Make Roster Moves to Reach 53-Man Roster Limit|url=https://www.patriots.com/news/patriots-make-roster-moves-to-reach-53-man-roster-limit|website=Patriots.com|date=August 30, 2022}}</ref>

===Indianapolis Colts===
On September 1, 2022, Hambright was signed to the [[Indianapolis Colts]]' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Colts Sign G Arlington Hambright, LB Segun Olubi To Practice Squad|url=https://www.colts.com/news/arlington-hambright-lb-segun-olubi-signed-practice-squad-guard-linebacker|website=Colts.com|date=September 1, 2022}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract on January 9, 2023.<ref>{{cite web|title=Colts Sign 12 To Reserve/Future Contracts, 2 To One-Year Contract Extensions|url=https://www.colts.com/news/deon-jackson-contract-extension-marcel-dabo-trevor-denbow-reserve-future|website=Colts.com|date=January 9, 2023}}</ref>

On August 31, 2023, Hambright was waived by the Colts and re-signed to the practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Colts sign DE Jake Martin, waive G Arlington Hambright; sign WR Racey McMath to practice squad, release CB Kevin Toliver II from practice squad|url=https://www.colts.com/news/jake-martin-signed-racey-mcmath-wide-receiver-practice-squad-roster-moves|website=Colts.com|date=August 31, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Colts sign G Arlington Hambright to the practice squad, release T Dan Skipper from the practice squad|url=https://www.colts.com/news/colts-sign-g-arlington-hambright-to-the-practice-squad-release-t-dan-skipper|website=Colts.com|date=September 4, 2023}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on September 19.<ref>{{cite web|title= We have signed G Arlington Hambright to the 53-man roster from the practice squad, signed RB Trey Sermon to the practice squad, and waived T Ryan Hayes.|url= https://www.colts.com/news/colts-sign-g-arlington-hambright-to-the-53-man-roster-from-the-practice-squad-si |website=Colts.com|date=September 19, 2023}}</ref> Hambright was released on December 14 and re-signed to the practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 14, 2023 |title=Colts sign WR D.J. Montgomery to 53-man roster from practice squad, waive G Arlington Hambright |url=https://colts.com/news/colts-sign-wr-d-j-montgomery-to-53-man-roster-from-practice-squad-waive-g-arling |access-date=15 December 2023 |website=Colts.com}}</ref> On January 8, 2024, he signed a reserve/future contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.colts.com/news/colts-sign-9-to-reserve-future-contracts-4-to-one-year-contract-extensions-waive|work=Colts.com|title=Colts sign 9 to reserve/future contracts, 4 to one-year contract extensions, waive CB Tony Brown|date=January 8, 2024|accessdate=January 10, 2024|author=Colts Communications}}</ref>

Hambright was waived by the Colts on August 27.<ref>{{cite web|title=Colts make roster moves to form initial 53-man roster for 2024 regular season|url=https://www.colts.com/news/jason-bean-evan-hull-jaylin-simpson-micah-abraham-roster-cuts-moves-jelani-woods-injured-reserve-53-man-roster|website=Colts.com|date=August 27, 2024}}</ref> He played in two games with the Colts during the [[2023 Indianapolis Colts season|2023 season]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Arlington Hambright 2023 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/H/HambAr00/gamelog/2023/ |access-date=2025-01-06 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

===Houston Texans===
On September 9, 2024, Hambright signed with the [[Houston Texans]]' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Texans sign Arlington Hambright to practice squad, release Cole Fotheringham|url=https://www.click2houston.com/sports/2024/09/09/texans-sign-arlington-hambright-to-practice-squad-release-cole-fotheringham/|website=Click 2 Houston|date=September 9, 2024}}</ref> He was released on October 22.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Wilson |first1=Aaron |title=Texans sign Jawhar Jordan to practice squad, release Rashad Weaver |url=https://www.click2houston.com/sports/2024/10/22/texans-sign-jawhar-jordan-to-practice-squad-release-rashad-weaver/ |website=Click2Houston.com |access-date=10 April 2026}}</ref>

===Tennessee Titans===
On October 29, 2024, Hambright was signed to the [[Tennessee Titans]]' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Titans Waive WR Mason Kinsey from 53-Man Roster, Add Three Players to the Team's Practice Squad|url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-waive-wr-mason-kinsey-from-53-man-roster-add-three-players-to-the-team-s-practice-squad|author=Wyatt, Jim|website=TennesseeTitans.com|date=October 29, 2024}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on December 28.<ref>{{cite web|title=Titans Make a Flurry of Roster Moves Ahead of Sunday's Game vs Jaguars|url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-make-a-flurry-of-roster-moves-ahead-of-sunday-s-game-vs-jaguars|author=Wyatt, Jim|website=TennesseeTitans.com|date=December 28, 2024}}</ref> Hambright played four games on [[special teams]] during the [[2024 Tennessee Titans season|2024 season]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Arlington Hambright 2024 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/H/HambAr00/gamelog/2024/ |access-date=2025-01-06 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

On April 29, 2025, Hambright was waived by the Titans.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Wyatt |first1=Jim |title=Roster Moves: Titans Waive Offensive Linemen Isaiah Prince, Arlington Hambright |url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/roster-moves-titans-waive-offensive-linemen-isaiah-prince-arlington-hambright |website=tennesseetitans.com |access-date=30 April 2025}}</ref> He was re-signed on August 3,<ref>{{cite web|title=Titans Sign OL Arlington Hambright, Waive WR Ramel Keyton|url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-sign-ol-arlington-hambright-waive-wr-ramel-keyton|author=Wyatt, Jim|website=TennesseeTitans.com|date=August 3, 2025}}</ref> and released on August 25 as part of final roster cuts.<ref>{{cite web|title=Titans Part Ways With 16 Players Ahead of Tuesday's Deadline|url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-part-ways-with-16-players-ahead-of-tuesday-s-deadline|author=Wyatt, Jim|website=TennesseeTitans.com|date=August 25, 2025}}</ref>

===Montreal Alouettes===
On February 19, 2026, Hambright signed with the [[Montreal Alouettes]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://3downnation.com/2026/02/19/montreal-alouettes-sign-former-nfl-draft-pick-arlington-hambright-one-other/|title=Montreal Alouettes sign former NFL Draft pick Arlington Hambright, one other|website=3DownNaton|date=February 19, 2026|access-date=February 22, 2026}}</ref> 

On April 9, 2026 Hambright announced his retirement from professional football.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Heilman |first1=Michael |title=Montreal Alouettes place offensive lineman Arlington Hambright on the retired list |url=https://www.bgmsportstrax.com/2026/04/09/montreal-alouettes-place-offensive-lineman-arlington-hambright-on-the-retired-list/ |website=BGMSportsTrax.com |access-date=10 April 2026}}</ref>

'''Arnold Rene Campbell''' (born November 13, 1962) is an American former professional [[Gridiron football|football]] [[defensive end]] who played one season for the [[Buffalo Bills]] in 1987.<ref name="PFR">{{Cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CampAr20.htm|title=Arnold Campbell Stats|website=www.pro-football-reference.com|accessdate=December 29, 2020}}</ref> He was a replacement player. He also played in the [[Arena Football League]] (AFL) and [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL).

==Early life==
Arnold Campbell was born on November 13, 1962, in [[Charleston, Mississippi]] and attended at [[Charleston High School (Mississippi)|Charleston High School]].<ref name=PFR/>

==College career==
He went to college at [[Alcorn State Braves football|Alcorn State]]<ref name=PFR/>

==Professional career==

===Buffalo Bills===
Campbell was a replacement player for the [[1987 Buffalo Bills season|Buffalo Bills]].<ref name=PFR/><ref name="JSS">{{Cite web|url=https://www.justsportsstats.com/footballstatsindex.php?player_id=campbarn001|title=Arnold Campbell Statistics on StatsCrew.com|website=www.StatsCrew.com|accessdate=December 29, 2020}}</ref> He played three games.<ref name=PFR/><ref name=JSS/>

===Ottawa Rough Riders===
In 1989, he played two games for the [[Ottawa Rough Riders]].<ref name=JSS/><ref name="PFA">{{Cite web|url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/playerc/camp01000.html|title=Arnold Campbell Stats – Pro Football Archives|website=www.profootballarchives.com|accessdate=December 29, 2020}}</ref> He was a defensive tackle.<ref name=PFA/>

===Detroit Drive===
In 1990 he played for the [[Detroit Drive]] of the [[Arena Football League]].<ref name=JSS/><ref name="arena">{{Cite web|url=https://www.arenafan.com/players/?page=players&player=252&pageview=career|title=Arnold Campbell - ArenaFan.com|website=www.arenafan.com|accessdate=December 29, 2020}}</ref> In 12 games he had 12 tackles and one fumble recovery.<ref name=JSS/><ref name=arena/>

===Orlando Predators===
In 1991 he played for two teams, the [[Orlando Predators]] and the [[Dallas Texans (Arena)|Dallas Texans]].<ref name=JSS/><ref name=arena/> With the Predators, he had four tackles in five games.<ref name=JSS/><ref name=arena/> He also had one sack.<ref name=JSS/>

===Dallas Texans===
His second team of 1991 was the [[Dallas Texans (Arena)|Dallas Texans]].<ref name=JSS/><ref name=arena/> With the Texans he had one tackle, he also had a sack in two games.<ref name=JSS/><ref name=arena/>

In 1992 he had 10 tackles in 10 games and two sacks.<ref name=JSS/><ref name=arena/> Campbell also had two forced fumbles and three recoveries.<ref name=JSS/><ref name=arena/>

===Arizona Rattlers===

In 1993, Campbell played for the [[Arizona Rattlers]].<ref name=JSS/><ref name=arena/> He had four sacks and 11 tackles.<ref name=arena/> He was in the Arena All-Star game. He played in 11 games.<ref name=JSS/><ref name=arena/>

===Milwaukee Mustangs (first stint)===

In 1994, he played for the [[Milwaukee Mustangs (1994–2001)|Milwaukee Mustangs]], he played in 10 games and had 15 tackles.<ref name=JSS/><ref name=arena/> He also had three forced fumbles.<ref name=JSS/><ref name=arena/>

===Miami Hooters===
He also played two games for the [[Miami Hooters]] in 1994 but he did not have any statistics.<ref name=JSS/><ref name=arena/>

He played in four games for the Miami Hooters in 1995.<ref name=JSS/> He had seven tackles before going back to the Milwaukee Mustangs.<ref name=JSS/><ref name=arena/> He had a blocked kick in 1995 for the Hooters.<ref name=JSS/><ref name=arena/>

===Milwaukee Mustangs (second stint)===
He had a second stint with the Mustangs in 1995; he played seven games and had six tackles and a sack.<ref name=JSS/><ref name=arena/> He also had a blocked kick, his second of the season.<ref name=JSS/><ref name=arena/>

In 1996 he played 14 games, the most of any season of his career.<ref name=JSS/><ref name=arena/> He had 12 tackles and five sacks; Campbell had eight passes defended also.<ref name=JSS/><ref name=arena/>

His final season was in 1997; he played 14 games again and had 15 tackles.<ref name=JSS/><ref name=arena/> He also had a sack and a fumble recovery.<ref name=JSS/><ref name=arena/>

'''Armon Merrell Hatcher''' (born July 15, 1976) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive back]] for one season with the [[San Diego Chargers]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Oregon State Beavers football|Oregon State Beavers]].

==Early life and college==
Armon Hatcher was born on July 15, 1976, in [[Diamond Bar, California]]. He went to high school there before playing [[college football]] at [[Oregon State University]]. He spent five years with the [[Oregon State Beavers football|Beavers]], redshirting his first year and [[Varsity letter|lettering]] as a safety the next four seasons. He played in all 44 games over four seasons, making 222 tackles and 13 interceptions, including one returned for a touchdown.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/armon-hatcher-1.html|title=Armon Hatcher College Stats|website=College Football at Sports-Reference.com}}</ref> His 13 interceptions ranked 2nd in Oregon State history.<ref name="auto1">{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/81498397/democrat-and-chronicle/|newspaper=[[Democrat and Chronicle]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=April 19, 1999|title=Untitled}} {{Open access}}</ref> In addition to playing defense, he was the team's kick returner, leading the [[Pac-12 Conference|Pac-10 Conference]] for returns in 1996.<ref name="auto"/> He received a bachelor's degree in business administration in 1999.

==Professional career==

Hatcher was selected by the [[Buffalo Bills]] as the 194th pick in the sixth round of the [[1999 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=1999 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1999/draft.htm |access-date=2023-03-29 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> Even though he played [[strong safety]] in all four of his college seasons, he was converted to [[free safety]] upon joining the Bills.<ref name="auto1"/> He was released at roster cuts.

He was signed by the [[BC Lions]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL) on June 16, 2000.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/81498879/the-province/|newspaper=[[The Province]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=June 18, 2000|title=Hatcher added}} {{Open access}}</ref> He was released a week later.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/81499028/red-deer-advocate/|newspaper=[[Red Deer Advocate]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=June 24, 2000|title=Untitled}} {{Open access}}</ref>

Later in the year he was signed by the [[San Diego Chargers]]. He spent most of the season on the practice squad, but did play in four games. In the first game, a 17–16 win over the [[Kansas City Chiefs]], Hatcher recorded one statistic, a five-yard penalty.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/H/HatcAr20/penalties/|title=Armon Hatcher Career Penalties|website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref> The game would be his only NFL win, as his next three games (and every other Chargers game in the season) were each losses.<ref name="auto2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/H/HatcAr20/gamelog/|title=Armon Hatcher Career Game Log|website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref> He was given the most playing time in a week 17 loss against the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]], where he recorded 3 tackles.<ref name="auto2"/>

Hatcher was sent to [[NFL Europe]] the following year, playing in ten games for the [[Amsterdam Admirals]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/playerh/hatc00300.html|website=www.profootballarchives.com|title=Armon Hatcher Stats - Pro Football Archives}}</ref> He made 34 tackles with the Admirals.

He was released by the Chargers at roster cuts in 2001.

His final team was the [[Frankfurt Galaxy (NFL Europe)|Frankfurt Galaxy]] in 2002. He appeared in ten games for the NFL Europe team, making 24 tackles. He also scored his only career touchdown with them, on a 100-yard return against the [[Barcelona Dragons (NFL Europe)|Barcelona Dragons]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/81499392/the-times-herald/|newspaper=[[The Times Herald]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=April 21, 2002|title=Hatcher, Alexander lift Galaxy to easy victory}} {{Open access}}</ref>

==Personal life==
His cousin, [[Billy Hatcher]], spent 11 seasons in [[Major League Baseball]] (MLB).<ref name="auto1"/>

After Hatcher's sports career he operated a marketing company from 2002 to 2009. He became a coach at [[Ohio Northern University]] in August 2009. He was given the assistant defensive backs coach position as well as the freshmen team defensive coordinator role.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://adaherald.com/Content/Social/Social/Article/Armon-Hatcher-picked-as-Assistant-Football-Coach-at-ONU/-2/-2/102293|title=Armon Hatcher picked as Assistant Football Coach at ONU|website=Ada Herald}}</ref>

'''Armani Lee Rogers''' (born December 4, 1997) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[tight end]] for the [[Houston Gamblers (UFL)|Houston Gamblers]] of the [[United Football League (2024)|United Football League]] (UFL). He played [[college football]] as a [[quarterback]] for the [[UNLV Rebels football|UNLV Rebels]] and [[Ohio Bobcats football|Ohio Bobcats]] and holds the record for longest run by an NCAA quarterback at 99 yards. Rogers transitioned to tight end after his college career and signed with the [[Washington Commanders]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2022.

==Early life==
The son of former NFL linebacker [[Sam Rogers (linebacker)|Sam Rogers]], Armani was born on December 4, 1997, in [[Buffalo, New York]].<ref name="TheBeast">{{cite web |last1=Brugler |first1=Dane |title=The Beast: 2022 NFL Draft Guide |url=https://cdn.theathletic.com/app/uploads/2022/04/07001122/2022_TheBeast_NFL_Draft_Guide.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220407122241/https://cdn.theathletic.com/app/uploads/2022/04/07001122/2022_TheBeast_NFL_Draft_Guide.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-date=April 7, 2022 |website=[[The Athletic]] |access-date=April 22, 2022 |pages=93 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> He grew up in [[Los Angeles]] and attended [[Alexander Hamilton High School (Los Angeles)|Alexander Hamilton High School]], Armani has four brothers and one sister where he passed for 1,433 yards and 18 touchdowns while rushing for 431 yards and six touchdowns as a senior.<ref name="decide">{{Cite web |last=Dewey |first=Todd |date=January 27, 2016 |title=Three-star QB recruit to decide today between UNLV, Fresno State |url=https://www.reviewjournal.com/sports/unlv/unlv-football/three-star-qb-recruit-to-decide-today-between-unlv-fresno-state/ |access-date=March 24, 2022 |website=[[Las Vegas Review-Journal]]}}</ref> Rogers was rated a three-star recruit and initially committed to play college football at California over offers from UCLA, Washington, and Utah.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sondheimer |first=Eric |date=February 23, 2015 |title=Football: Hamilton QB Armani Rogers commits to Cal |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/highschool/varsity-times/la-sp-vi-football-hamilton-qb-armani-rogers-commits-to-cal-20150223-story.html |access-date=April 13, 2022 |website=[[Los Angeles Times]]}}</ref> He decommitted during his senior year following changes to California's coaching staff and later signed to play at UNLV after considering Fresno State.<ref name=decide/>

==College career==

Rogers began his college career at the [[University of Nevada, Las Vegas]] and redshirted as a freshman.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Grimala |first=Mike |date=September 2, 2017 |title=All eyes on Armani: How 'The Franchise' became UNLV football's best hope |url=https://lasvegassun.com/news/2017/sep/02/all-eyes-on-armani-how-the-franchise-became-unlv-f/ |access-date=March 23, 2022 |website=[[Las Vegas Sun]]}}</ref> He started nine games for the Rebels during his redshirt [[2017 UNLV Rebels football team|freshman season]] and was named the [[Mountain West Conference]] Freshman of the Year after completing 99 of 189 pass attempts for 1,471 yards and six touchdowns with five interceptions and setting a school record for rushing yards by a quarterback with 780 and also rushing for eight touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Anderson |first=Mark |date=November 29, 2017 |title=UNLV's Armani Rogers, Lexington Thomas honored by MW yards and 10 touchdowns and 565 rushing yards and eight touchdowns.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://athlonsports.com/college-football/mountain-west-quarterback-rankings-2019|title=2019 Mountain West Quarterback Rankings|first=Steven|last=Lassan|website=[[Athlon Sports]]|date=May 9, 2019|access-date=April 13, 2022}}</ref> He passed for 393 yards with two touchdowns and three interceptions and ===Ohio Bobcats===
Rogers transferred to [[Ohio Bobcats football|Ohio]] as a graduate student.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Grimala |first=Mike |date=July 6, 2020 |title=Former starting QB Armani Rogers transferring from UNLV |url=https://lasvegassun.com/news/2020/jul/06/armani-rogers-transferring-from-unlv/ |access-date=March 23, 2022 |website=[[Las Vegas Sun]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Gordon |first=Sam |date=July 14, 2020 |title=UNLV QB Armani Rogers transfers to Ohio University |url=https://www.reviewjournal.com/sports/unlv/unlv-football/unlv-qb-armani-rogers-transfers-to-ohio-university-2073611/ |access-date=March 23, 2022 |website=[[Las Vegas Review-Journal]]}}</ref> In [[2020 Ohio Bobcats football team|2020]], he was used mostly in [[Package (American football)|offensive package plays]] and threw for 48 yards and a touchdown while rushing for 114 yards and two touchdowns.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://projects.thepostathens.com/SpecialProjects/orientation-guide-2021/ohio-football-2021-quarterback-question.html|title=FOOTBALL: OHIO'S QUARTERBACK QUESTION|first=Jack|last=Gleckler|work=[[The Post (Ohio student newspaper)|The Post]]|date=May 27, 2021|access-date=April 4, 2022}}</ref> Rogers used the extra year of eligibility granted to college athletes in 2020 due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]] and returned to Ohio for a second season. '''Arron Mosby''' (born April 13, 1999) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[linebacker]] for the [[Green Bay Packers]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Fresno State Bulldogs football|Fresno State Bulldogs]] and was signed by the [[Carolina Panthers]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2022.

==Early life and education==
Mosby was born on April 13, 1999, in [[Fresno, California]]. He attended [[Sanger High School (California)|Sanger High School]] and was a two-way starter, playing at [[wide receiver]] on offense and [[cornerback]] on defense. He was twice named all-league as a [[defensive back]] and was given first-team all-CMAC honors in 2016 as a [[Senior (education)|senior]]. That year, he was named a ''[[Fresno Bee]]'' all-star.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web |title=Arron Mosby |url=https://gobulldogs.com/sports/football/roster/arron-mosby/10540 |access-date=March 11, 2023 |website=[[Fresno State Bulldogs]]}}</ref>

After graduating from Sanger, Mosby committed to [[Fresno State University]] and played in every game as a true [[freshman]], mainly as a [[special teamer]]. He made a total of five [[Tackle (football move)|tackles]] in 14 games. As a [[sophomore]] in 2018, Mosby recorded 12 tackles and one [[interception]] while appearing in 13 out of 14 games. His one interception was returned 95 yards for a [[touchdown]] against [[San Jose State Spartans football|San Jose State]] and was the fourth-longest in team history.<ref name="auto" />

Mosby recorded 78 tackles as a [[Junior (education year)|junior]] in 2019, placing fourth on the squad. He appeared in all 12 games, and 40 of his tackles were solo stops. In a 2020 season shortened by [[COVID-19]], Mosby played in all six games and recorded 21 tackles, including three for a loss. All players were given an extra year of eligibility because of the virus, and he opted to return to the team in 2021 as a fifth-year player. Playing [[defensive end]], Mosby started 12 games out of 13 and was named an honorable mention All-[[Mountain West Conference]]. He recorded 40 tackles, six [[quarterback sack|sacks]], six forced [[fumble]]s, two recoveries, and a team-leading 15.5 tackles-for-loss. He was invited to the [[Hula Bowl]] and the [[NFLPA]] All-Star Game after the season ended.<ref name="auto" />

===Green Bay Packers===
On August 3, 2023, Mosby was claimed off waivers by the [[Green Bay Packers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Packers claim LB Arron Mosby|url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-claim-lb-arron-mosby|website=Packers.com|date=August 3, 2023}}</ref> He was released on August 29.<ref>{{cite web |title=Packers announce roster moves|url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-announce-roster-moves-2023-nfl-season|publisher=packers.com |access-date=August 29, 2023}}</ref> A day later, he was signed to the Packers' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web |title=Packers sign 16 players to practice squad|url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-sign-16-players-to-practice-squad-2023|publisher=packers.com |access-date=August 30, 2023}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract with Green Bay on January 22, 2024.<ref>{{cite web|title=Packers sign 14 free agents|url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-sign-14-free-agents-jan-22-2024|website=Packers.com|date=January 22, 2024}}</ref>

On August 24, 2024, in the preseason finale against the [[Baltimore Ravens]], Mosby strip-sacked rookie quarterback [[Devin Leary]], which was recovered by teammate [[Anthony Johnson Jr.]] for a touchdown. On the very next drive, he picked off Leary on a short pass. His performance ultimately landed him a spot on the Packers' initial 53-man roster ahead of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kuhagen |first=Christopher |title=Who is Arron Mosby? '''Arnold Lee Brown''' (born August 27, 1962) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive back]] for two seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) with the [[Detroit Lions]] and [[Seattle Seahawks]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[North Carolina Central Eagles football|North Carolina Central Eagles]] and was selected by the Seahawks in the fifth round of the [[1985 NFL draft]]. He was also a member of the [[Denver Broncos]].

==Early life and college==
Arnold Lee Brown was born in [[Wilmington, North Carolina]].<ref name="Pfa"/> He attended [[Emsley A. Laney High School]] in Wilmington.<ref name="Pfa"/> In college, he was a four-year [[letterman (sports)|letterman]] for the [[North Carolina Central Eagles football|North Carolina Central Eagles]] from 1981 to 1984.<ref name="Pfa">{{cite web | url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/players/b/brow00800.html | title=Arnold Brown | publisher=Pro Football Archives | accessdate=24 December 2024}}</ref>

==Profesional career==
Brown was selected by the [[Seattle Seahawks]] in the fifth round, with the 128th overall pick, of the [[1985 NFL draft]].<ref name="Pfr"/> He officially signed with the team on July 21.<ref name="transactions"/> He was released on August 27, 1985.<ref name="transactions"/>

Brown signed with the [[Detroit Lions]] on September 10, 1985.<ref name="transactions"/> He played in seven games for the Lions during the 1985 season before being placed on injured reserve on November 2, 1985.<ref name="transactions"/><ref name="Pfr"/> He was placed on injured reserve again the following year on August 22, 1986, and spent the entire season there.<ref name="transactions"/> He was released on August 26, 1987.<ref name="transactions"/>

Brown was signed by the [[Seattle Seahawks]] on October 9, 1987, during the [[1987 NFL players strike]].<ref name="transactions"/> He appeared in two games for the Seahawks before being released on October 20, 1987, after the strike ended.<ref name="Pfr">{{cite web | url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BrowAr20.htm | title=Arnold Brown | publisher=Pro Football Reference | accessdate=24 December 2024}}</ref><ref name="transactions"/>

Brown signed with the [[Denver Broncos]] on March 28, 1998.<ref name="transactions"/> He was released on July 18, 1988.<ref name="transactions">{{cite web | url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/transactions/b/brow00800.html | title=Arnold Brown NFL Transactions | publisher=Pro Football Archives | accessdate=24 December 2024}}</ref>

'''Armand Membou''' ({{respell|MEM|boo}}; born March 27, 2004) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[offensive tackle]] for the [[New York Jets]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Missouri Tigers football|Missouri Tigers]] and was selected by the Jets seventh overall in the [[2025 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Membou was born on March 27, 2004 in [[Lee's Summit, Missouri]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Prashack |first=Derek |date=2025-05-03 |title=Everything you need to know about NY Jets rookie OT Armand Membou |url=https://thejetpress.com/everything-need-know-ny-jets-rookie-armand-membou-01jt29q88hh0 |access-date=2026-03-05 |website=The Jet Press|publisher=FanSided |language=en-US}}</ref> He later attended [[Lee's Summit North High School]]. He was rated as a four-star recruit and committed to play [[college football]] for the [[Missouri Tigers football|Missouri Tigers]] over numerous Power 4 offers.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Williams |first1=Sean |title=Armand Membou is Mizzou's latest commitment |url=https://missouri.rivals.com/news/armand-membou-is-mizzou-s-latest-commitment |website=Rivals.com |date=27 March 2021 |access-date=November 16, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Stava |first1=Sammy |title=Missouri Football Recruiting: Mizzou lands Lee's Summit North Offensive Guard Armand Membou |url=https://www.rockmnation.com/2021/3/27/22354170/missouri-tigers-football-recruiting-2022-class-armand-membou-lees-summit |website=Rock M Nation |date=27 March 2021 |access-date=November 16, 2024}}</ref>

==College career==
During Membou's first two seasons in 2022 and 2023, he appeared in 24 games with 18 starts for the Tigers at right tackle, where in 2023 he was a full-time starter on the Tigers line, which finished as a Joe Moore award semifinalist.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Soble |first1=Jack |title='Success story': Inside Membou's rise to starting on Missouri's offensive line '''Arman T. Shields''' (born July 10, 1985) is an American former [[American football|football]] [[wide receiver]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Richmond Spiders football|Richmond Spiders]], and was selected by the [[Oakland Raiders]] in the fourth round of the [[2008 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Arman T. Shields was born on July 10, 1985.<ref name="Pfa">{{cite web | url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/players/s/shie00300.html#gsc.tab=0 | title=Arman Shields | publisher=Pro Football Archives | accessdate=23 March 2026}}</ref> He attended [[Gonzaga College High School]] in [[Washington, D.C.]]<ref name="Pfa"/>

==College career==
Shield played [[college football]] for the [[Richmond Spiders football|Richmond Spiders]] of the [[University of Richmond]] from 2004 to 2007.<ref name="Pfa"/> He was [[redshirted]] in 2003.<ref name="Pfa"/> He earned second-team All-[[Atlantic 10 Conference]] honors in 2006 after catching five touchdowns.<ref name="Sign">{{cite web | url=https://richmondspiders.com/sports/2008/7/24/205205994 | title=Arman Shields Signs With Oakland | publisher=[[University of Richmond]] | date=July 24, 2008 | accessdate=23 March 2026}}</ref> As a senior in 2007, he recorded 12 receptions for 107 yards in the season opener.<ref name="Packett">{{cite news | url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/richmond-times-dispatch/194063115/ | title=A chance from Santa | work=[[Richmond Times-Dispatch]] | date=February 20, 2008 | accessdate=23 March 2026 | author=Packett, John | pages=C2}}</ref> However, he suffered a [[torn PCL]] the next week.<ref name="Packett"/> He briefly returned for one [[Series (American football)|series]] in an October game before missing the rest of the season due to the injury.<ref name="Packett"/> Shields finished his college career with 160 catches for 1,930 yards and 13 touchdowns.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-tribune/194063041/ | title=Raiders trade away Washington | work=[[The Tribune (San Luis Obispo)|The Tribune]] | date=April 28, 2008 | accessdate=23 March 2026 | pages=S3}}</ref> His receptions total was the second most in school history.<ref name="Combine">{{cite web | url=https://richmondspiders.com/news/2008/2/29/205202115 | title=Arman Shields Puts Up Big Numbers At 2008 NFL Combine | publisher=[[University of Richmond]] | date=February 29, 2008 | accessdate=23 March 2026}}</ref>

==Professional career==
Shields was the first Richmond player invited to the [[NFL Combine]] since [[Shawn Barber (American football)|Shawn Barber]] in 1998.<ref name="Packett"/> Shields was one of the fastest players at the Combine, posting a 4.37 second [[40-yard dash]].<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-free-lance-star/194063463/ | title=More state players chosen | work=[[The Free Lance-Star]] | date=April 28, 2008 | agency=[[Associated Press]] | accessdate=23 March 2026 | pages=B2}}</ref> He had the best [[20-yard shuttle]] (3.96 s) and the best 60-yard shuttle (10.87 s).<ref name="Combine"/> He was selected by the [[Oakland Raiders]] in the fourth round, with the 125th overall pick, of the [[2008 NFL draft]].<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-sacramento-bee/194063564/ | title=Washington is traded to Ravens | work=[[The Sacramento Bee]] | date=April 28, 2008 | accessdate=23 March 2026 | author=Jones, Jason | pages=C6}}</ref> ''[[The Daytona Beach News-Journal]]'' noted that Shields was a "surprising choice after fewer than 2,000 career yards and a serious injury."<ref>{{cite news | | author=Chapman, Alex | pages=3B}}</ref> The ''[[Oakland Tribune]]'' said that Shields was a "typical boom-or-bust, 'measurables' pick by owner [[Al Davis]]",<ref name="nbc">{{cite web | Shields missed most of spring practices in 2008 with a lower body injury.<ref name="nbc"/> He signed with the Raiders on July 23, 2008.<ref name="Sign"/> Davis gave Shields a $425K signing bonus.<ref name="nbc"/> On August 30, 2008, Shields was placed on injured reserve due to a knee injury.<ref name="Pfa"/> He ended up missing the entire [[2008 NFL season]].<ref name="Pfa"/> On May 9, 2009, it was reported that Shields had not yet fully recovered from the injury.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/san-francisco-chronicle/194063932/ | title=Walker surprised team with surgery | work=[[San Francisco Chronicle]] | date=May 9, 2009 | accessdate=23 March 2026 | author=White, David | pages=D8}}</ref> He was released by the Raiders on July 29, 2009, after failing a physical.<ref name="Pfa"/> In May 2010, he participated in rookie [[minicamp]] on a tryout basis with the [[Atlanta Falcons]].<ref name="nbc"/>

==Personal life==
Shields' father, Bertie Shields, was a Guyanan immigrant who served in the [[United States Army]].<ref name="Carpenter">{{cite news | url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/sports/2008/04/23/a-son-a-chance-a-dream/e38a3197-172d-4f3c-949e-1db5a08d607b/ | title=A Son, a Chance, a Dream | work=[[The Washington Post]] | date=April 22, 2008 | accessdate=24 March 2026 | author=Carpenter, Les}}</ref> While stationed in South Korea in 1975, he was tasked with walking one mile through the [[Korean Demilitarized Zone]] to spy through the fence.<ref name="Carpenter"/> Arman Shields became a real estate agent after his football career.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.desertlionproperty.com/arman-shields | title=Arman Shields | publisher=Desert Lion Property | accessdate=23 March 2026}}</ref>
